XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Yn y fersiwn ddwyieithog, mae’r golofn chwith yn cynnwys yr iaith a lefarwyd yn y cyfarfod. Mae’r golofn dde yn cynnwys cyfieithiad o’r areithiau hynny.

Mae [R] yn dynodi bod yr Aelod wedi datgan buddiant wrth gyflwyno’r busnes.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
In the bilingual version, the left-hand column includes the language used during the meeting. The right-hand column includes a translation of those speeches.

[R] indicates that the Member has declared an interest when tabling the business.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Cyfarfu'r Senedd yn y Siambr a thrwy gynhadledd fideo am 13:30 gyda'r Llywydd (Huw Irranca-Davies) yn y Gadair.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: The Senedd met in the Chamber and by video-conference at 13:30 with the Llywydd (Huw Irranca-Davies) in the Chair.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: Datganiad gan y Llywydd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: Statement by the Llywydd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Prynhawn da, bawb.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Good afternoon, everybody.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: Datganiad gan y Llywydd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: Statement by the Llywydd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Good afternoon, everybody. We will make a start.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Prynhawn da, bawb. Fe wnawn ni gychwyn arni.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: Datganiad gan y Llywydd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: Statement by the Llywydd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Gadewch inni ddechrau. Yn gyntaf, hoffwn roi gwybod i'r Aelodau, yn unol â Rheol Sefydlog 26.87, fy mod wedi sefydlu a chyhoeddi amserlen ar gyfer balotau Biliau Aelod ar gyfer y seithfed Senedd. Cynhelir dau falot, y cyntaf ddydd Mercher 14 Hydref a'r ail ddydd Mercher 7 Gorffennaf 2027. Mae'r broses ar gyfer balotau Biliau Aelod yn newydd ar gyfer y seithfed Senedd. Am y tro cyntaf, bydd y rhain yn falotau enw yn unig. Bydd rhagor o fanylion am y balotau, ynghyd â gwybodaeth am yr hyfforddiant a fydd ar gael ar y broses o ran Biliau Aelod, yn cael eu cyhoeddi i'r holl Aelodau yr wythnos hon. Diolch.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Let's make a start. I would first of all like to inform Members that, in accordance with Standing Order 26.87, I have established and published the timetable for the Member Bill ballots for the seventh Senedd. Two ballots will be held, the first on Wednesday 14 October and the second on Wednesday 7 July 2027. The process for Member Bill ballots is new for the seventh Senedd. For the first time, these will be name-only ballots. Further detail about the ballots, together with information about the training that will be available on the Member Bill process, will be issued to all Members this week. Thank you.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Nawr, symudwn i eitem 1, cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog. Cwestiwn 1, Cai Parry-Jones.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Now, we will move on to item 1, questions to the First Minister. The first question is from Cai Parry-Jones.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Arbedion Cost
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Cost Savings

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: 1. A yw Llywodraeth Cymru wedi gwneud unrhyw arbedion cost diriaethol mewn unrhyw adran yn ystod y Senedd hon hyd yn hyn? OQ64428
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: 1. Has the Welsh Government made any tangible cost savings in any department during this Senedd so far? OQ64428

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Llywydd, our job is to make every £1 work as hard as possible for the people of Wales. That means focusing resources on the priorities that matter most to people and delivering the commitments we were elected to deliver. We're reviewing spending across Government to ensure resources are directed where they can make the biggest difference, whether that's cutting waiting lists, tackling child poverty or strengthening our economy. Alongside this, we will continue to press Westminster, of course, for the fair funding that Wales deserves.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Lywydd, ein cyfrifoldeb ni yw gwneud i bob £1 weithio mor galed â phosibl i bobl Cymru. Mae hynny'n golygu canolbwyntio adnoddau ar y blaenoriaethau sydd bwysicaf i bobl a chyflawni'r ymrwymiadau y cawsom ni ein hethol i'w cyflawni. Rydym ni'n adolygu gwariant ar draws y Llywodraeth i sicrhau bod adnoddau yn cael eu cyfeirio lle gallan nhw wneud y gwahaniaeth mwyaf, pa un a yw hynny'n golygu torri rhestrau aros, mynd i'r afael â thlodi plant neu gryfhau ein heconomi. Ochr yn ochr â hyn, byddwn yn parhau i bwyso ar San Steffan, wrth gwrs, am y cyllid teg y mae Cymru yn ei haeddu.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
I'll take that as a 'no'. A key component of the Welsh Government's administrative spend is the estate it owns and manages. According to the most recent and cutely named 'State of the Estate' report, published in April, we see that the Welsh Government has around 70,000 sq m of estate at a cost of nearly £20 million a year. Seventy thousand square metres of estate is exactly the same as the 2020 target produced pre COVID and before the boom in home working. We also learnt from the latest report, quote:

'Most Staff continued to work remotely'.

First Minister, smarter management of the estate could save over £10 million a year. My question is: why is the Welsh Government not making these obvious efficiencies?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Fe wnaf i gymryd hynny fel 'nac ydy'. Un o elfennau allweddol gwariant gweinyddol Llywodraeth Cymru yw'r ystad y mae'n berchen arni ac yn ei rheoli. Yn ôl yr adroddiad 'Cyflwr yr Ystad' diweddaraf, a gyhoeddwyd ym mis Ebrill, rydym ni'n gweld bod gan Lywodraeth Cymru oddeutu 70,000 metr sgwâr o ystâd ar gost o bron i £20 miliwn y flwyddyn. Mae saith deg mil metr sgwâr o ystad yn union yr un fath â tharged 2020 a gynhyrchwyd cyn COVID a chyn y cynnydd enfawr i weithio gartref. Fe wnaethom ni hefyd ddarganfod o'r adroddiad diweddaraf, dyfyniad:

'Parhaodd y rhan fwyaf o'r staff i weithio o bell'.

Brif Weinidog, gallai rheoli'r ystad yn fwy clyfar arbed dros £10 miliwn y flwyddyn. Fy nghwestiwn i yw: pam nad yw Llywodraeth Cymru yn gwneud yr arbedion effeithlonrwydd amlwg hyn?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: I know the Member comes from the position of begrudgingly having even a square foot of estate in Wales looking after the interests of the people of Wales. But, I'll tell you what, this Government is a Government that believes in using the resources that we have wisely. We can look at it in terms of square footage or we can look at it in terms of people. What I want to do is make the most of the people that we have, whether that's working in the civil service, whether it's working across public sector, in health and education and in everything this Government does—including encouraging people to get the right balance between remote working and working in the office. We will do our utmost to make, as I say, the best use of every single £1. In that context, maybe he should take my original answer as a 'yes'.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Rwy'n gwybod bod yr Aelod yn dod o'r safbwynt o fod yn anfoddog â hyd yn oed troedfedd sgwâr o ystad yng Nghymru yn gofalu am fuddiannau pobl Cymru. Ond, ddywedaf i wrthych chi beth, mae'r Llywodraeth hon yn Llywodraeth sy'n credu mewn defnyddio'r adnoddau sydd gennym ni yn ddoeth. Gallwn ni ei ystyried o safbwynt troedfeddi sgwâr neu gallwn ni ei ystyried o safbwynt pobl. Yr hyn yr wyf i eisiau ei wneud yw gwneud y gorau o'r bobl sydd gennym ni, pa un a yw hynny'n gweithio yn y gwasanaeth sifil, yn gweithio ar draws y sector cyhoeddus, ym meysydd iechyd ac addysg ac ym mhopeth y mae'r Llywodraeth hon yn ei wneud—gan gynnwys annog pobl i gael y cydbwysedd cywir rhwng gweithio o bell a gweithio yn y swyddfa. Byddwn yn gwneud ein gorau glas i wneud, fel y dywedais i, y defnydd gorau o bob £1. Yn y cyd-destun hwnnw, efallai y dylai gymryd fy ateb gwreiddiol fel 'ydy'.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Yesterday, the Public Accounts and Public Administration Committee took evidence from Adrian Crompton, the outgoing Auditor General for Wales. In his evidence, he was clear that value for money is not just about spending less, it's about making the money we do have work better. If we are to address the real challenges facing our communities today, what we need to focus on is better Government, driven by a new leadership. I'm delighted that this is already a core commitment of this Government and something it's getting started on quickly in its first 100 days. Will the First Minister assure us that his Government will maintain a relentless focus on improving outcomes for people and making the best use of the resources that Government does have?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Ddoe, clywodd y Pwyllgor Cyfrifon Cyhoeddus a Gweinyddiaeth Gyhoeddus dystiolaeth gan Adrian Crompton, Archwilydd Cyffredinol Cymru sy'n gadael. Yn ei dystiolaeth, roedd yn eglur nad yw gwerth am arian yn golygu gwario llai yn unig, mae'n golygu gwneud i'r arian sydd gennym ni weithio'n well. Os ydym ni'n mynd i fynd i'r afael â'r heriau gwirioneddol sy'n wynebu ein cymunedau heddiw, yr hyn y mae angen i ni ganolbwyntio arno yw gwell Llywodraeth, wedi'i ysgogi gan arweinyddiaeth newydd. Rwyf i wrth fy modd bod hwn eisoes yn ymrwymiad craidd i'r Llywodraeth hon ac yn rhywbeth y mae'n cychwyn arno'n gyflym yn ei 100 diwrnod cyntaf. A wnaiff y Prif Weinidog ein sicrhau ni y bydd ei Lywodraeth yn parhau i ganolbwyntio'n ddiwyro ar wella canlyniadau i bobl a gwneud y defnydd gorau o'r adnoddau sydd gan y Llywodraeth?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: We've made it clear that it's all about outcomes, it's all about looking at how the decisions that we take as a Government impact positively on the lives of the people of Wales. I absolutely agree that good Government isn't about chasing short-term savings, if you like. Though we make every £1 work hard, it is about making every £1 deliver better outcomes for the people of Wales. It's why we're reforming how public services are delivered. That stronger focus on prevention is one that comes to mind immediately—how we can spend money now on stopping some of those problems in health occurring later down the line. It's why the target has been put in place by the enterprise Minister on halving the productivity gap and making the investment now in ensuring that we strengthen the economy in that way. It is all about good Government, with long-term positive outcomes for the people of Wales.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Rydym ni wedi ei gwneud hi'n eglur bod y cwbl yn fater o ganlyniadau, mae'r cwbl yn fater o edrych ar sut mae'r penderfyniadau yr ydym ni'n eu gwneud fel Llywodraeth yn effeithio'n gadarnhaol ar fywydau pobl Cymru. Rwy'n cytuno'n llwyr nad yw Llywodraeth dda yn golygu mynd ar drywydd arbedion byrdymor, fel petai. Er ein bod ni'n gwneud i bob £1 weithio'n galed, mae'n golygu gwneud i bob £1 sicrhau canlyniadau gwell i bobl Cymru. Dyna pam rydym ni'n diwygio sut mae gwasanaethau cyhoeddus yn cael eu darparu. Mae'r pwyslais cryfach hwnnw ar atal yn un sy'n dod i'r meddwl yn syth—sut y gallwn ni wario arian rŵan ar atal rhai o'r problemau hynny ym maes iechyd sy'n digwydd yn ddiweddarach. Dyna pam mae'r targed wedi cael ei gyflwyno gan y Gweinidog menter ar haneru'r bwlch cynhyrchiant a gwneud y buddsoddiad rŵan i sicrhau ein bod ni'n cryfhau'r economi yn y modd hwnnw. Mae'r cwbl yn fater o Lywodraeth dda, â chanlyniadau cadarnhaol hirdymor i bobl Cymru.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch, Brif Weinidog. One of the key challenges of Government is to manage in-year spend and in-year overspends. You will know, First Minister, that local government is bound by law that they have to balance their books within year. That doesn't go for other governmental departments. Do you accept the principle that all Government departments should manage their budgets to the agreed budgets, or, if not, can you outline what in-year overspends you are prepared to accept this year?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch, Brif Weinidog. Un o brif heriau Llywodraeth yw rheoli gwariant yn ystod y flwyddyn a gorwariant yn ystod y flwyddyn. Byddwch yn gwybod, Brif Weinidog, bod llywodraeth leol wedi'i rhwymo gan y gyfraith bod yn rhaid iddyn nhw fantoli eu cyfrifon o fewn y flwyddyn. Nid yw hynny'n wir i adrannau llywodraethol eraill. A ydych chi'n derbyn yr egwyddor y dylai pob adran Llywodraeth reoli eu cyllidebau yn unol â'r cyllidebau y cytunwyd arnyn nhw, neu, os nad ydych, a allwch chi amlinellu pa orwariant yn ystod y flwyddyn yr ydych chi'n barod i'w dderbyn eleni?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: The Member will imagine, I'm sure—and he'd imagine correctly—that this is a Government coming into power that is determined to look afresh at all the budgets that we have, to make sure they are aligned with our priorities, that money is being spent well, with outcomes at the heart of everything that we do. It's not the case that our Government departments can have overspends as such. There are elements of the public service, we know, where there are significant in-year pressures—health being one of those—and this Government has indeed inherited hundreds of millions of pounds of in-year pressures in the health service as a result of the mismanagement of health by previous Labour health Ministers. That's something that doesn't stop us from getting to grips with the challenge now in improving public services, but that is the reality, and everything we do is about making sure that our public funding is dealt with in a prudent way, to deliver the best outcomes for the people of Wales.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Bydd yr Aelod yn dychmygu, rwy'n siŵr—a byddai'n dychmygu'n gywir—bod hon yn Llywodraeth sy'n dod i rym sy'n benderfynol o edrych o'r newydd ar yr holl gyllidebau sydd gennym ni, i wneud yn siŵr eu bod nhw'n cyd-fynd â'n blaenoriaethau, bod arian yn cael ei wario'n dda, â chanlyniadau yn ganolog i bopeth yr ydym ni'n ei wneud. Nid yw'n wir y gall ein hadrannau Llywodraeth fod â gorwariant fel y cyfryw. Ceir elfennau o'r gwasanaeth cyhoeddus, rydym ni'n gwybod, lle ceir pwysau sylweddol yn ystod y flwyddyn—mae iechyd yn un o'r rheini—ac mae'r Llywodraeth hon yn wir wedi etifeddu cannoedd o filiynau o bunnoedd o bwysau yn ystod y flwyddyn yn y gwasanaeth iechyd o ganlyniad i gamreolaeth iechyd gan Weinidogion iechyd Llafur blaenorol. Mae hynny'n rhywbeth nad yw'n ein hatal rhag mynd i'r afael â'r her nawr o ran gwella gwasanaethau cyhoeddus, ond dyna'r realiti, ac mae popeth yr ydym ni'n ei wneud yn fater o sicrhau bod ein cyllid cyhoeddus yn cael ei drin mewn ffordd ddarbodus, i sicrhau'r canlyniadau gorau i bobl Cymru.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: First Minister, one of the inquiries that the Economy, Trade and Rural Affairs Committee undertook at the end of the last Senedd term was to look at the Global Centre of Rail Excellence. It was made clear to us that an incoming Government would have to make a critical decision over whether it was going to back this particular venture, and the tag price on that was some £400 million. No small change in the back of the sofa for that, I would suggest. Has the Government had a chance to formulate a view on the future funding requirements for the Global Centre of Rail Excellence, and, if you have, when will you be bringing a statement forward so that we know what the commitment will be, going forward?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Brif Weinidog, un o'r ymchwiliadau a gynhaliwyd gan Bwyllgor yr Economi, Masnach a Materion Gwledig ar ddiwedd y tymor Senedd diwethaf oedd edrych ar y Ganolfan Ragoriaeth Fyd-Eang ar gyfer Rheilffyrdd. Fe'i gwnaed hi'n eglur i ni y byddai'n rhaid i Lywodraeth newydd wneud penderfyniad critigol pa un a oedd yn mynd i gefnogi'r fenter benodol hon, a'r pris am hynny oedd tua £400 miliwn. Dim newid mân i lawr cefn y soffa ar gyfer hynny, byddwn i'n awgrymu. A yw'r Llywodraeth wedi cael cyfle i lunio safbwynt ar y gofynion ariannu ar gyfer y Ganolfan Ragoriaeth Fyd-Eang ar gyfer Rheilffyrdd yn y dyfodol, ac, os ydych chi, pryd fyddwch chi'n cyhoeddi datganiad fel ein bod ni'n gwybod beth fydd yr ymrwymiad yn y dyfodol?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: The Member is right to point to this as being something that can offer opportunities in terms of the Welsh economy, but he's also right to point out that there are significant expenditure commitments that would need to be made in order to get to that point. The Government has not yet come to a decision around that. That is a consideration that will be ongoing, and I'm unable to give a date on that. As the Member will be aware, there are many, many funding considerations that the Government is grappling with in these early weeks.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Mae'r Aelod yn iawn i gyfeirio at hyn fel rhywbeth a all gynnig cyfleoedd o ran economi Cymru, ond mae hefyd yn iawn i nodi bod ymrwymiadau gwariant sylweddol y byddai angen eu gwneud er mwyn cyrraedd y pwynt hwnnw. Nid yw'r Llywodraeth wedi gwneud penderfyniad ynglŷn â hynny eto. Mae honno'n ystyriaeth a fydd yn parhau, ac ni allaf roi dyddiad ar hynny. Fel y bydd yr Aelod yn gwybod, mae yna lawer iawn o ystyriaethau ariannu y mae'r Llywodraeth yn ymgodymu â nhw yn yr wythnosau cynnar hyn.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Amseroedd Aros
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Waiting Times

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: 2. Pa gamau y mae Llywodraeth Cymru yn eu cymryd i leihau amseroedd aros ar gyfer apwyntiadau cleifion allanol a llawdriniaethau i gleifion yn sir y Fflint a Wrecsam? OQ64369
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: 2. What action is the Welsh Government taking to reduce waiting times for out-patient appointments and surgery for patients in Flintshire and Wrexham? OQ64369

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: We announced an additional £145 million to support a clinically led approach to focus on delivering a sustainable solution to reducing waiting times and driving pathway transformation. We've set up an expert panel to look at the development of surgical hubs and are commissioning an independent review of performance and the impact waiting has on patients.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Fe wnaethom ni gyhoeddi £145 miliwn ychwanegol i gefnogi dull dan arweiniad clinigol i ganolbwyntio ar ddarparu ateb cynaliadwy i leihau amseroedd aros ac ysgogi trawsnewidiad llwybrau. Rydym ni wedi sefydlu panel arbenigol i edrych ar ddatblygiad canolfannau llawfeddygol ac yn comisiynu adolygiad annibynnol o berfformiad a'r effaith y mae aros yn ei chael ar gleifion.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Well, that doesn't help me, I'm afraid, First Minister. I've got a letter for an appointment here, actually, for myself personally, which was written a year ago, which tells me that I've been placed on an out-patient waiting list in Betsi Cadwaladr trust, and that I'd be contacted as soon as possible, and I've heard nothing since. I've also been told by someone else that they've been waiting three years—three years—for gallbladder surgery, and they've heard nothing since whatsoever. I could be dead by now. What are you actually doing, and what can you do for my constituent, so they can realistically expect to receive the appointment and treatment they've been waiting so long for? Diolch.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Wel, nid yw hynny'n fy helpu i, mae gen i ofn, Brif Weinidog. Mae gen i lythyr ar gyfer apwyntiad yma, a dweud y gwir, i mi fy hun yn bersonol, a ysgrifennwyd flwyddyn yn ôl, sy'n dweud wrthyf i fy mod wedi cael fy rhoi ar restr aros cleifion allanol yn ymddiriedolaeth Betsi Cadwaladr, ac y byddai rhywun yn cysylltu â mi cyn gynted â phosibl, ac nid wyf i wedi clywed dim ers hynny. Mae rhywun arall hefyd wedi dweud wrthyf i ei fod wedi bod yn aros tair blynedd—tair blynedd—am lawdriniaeth coden y bustl, ac nid yw wedi clywed dim o gwbl ers hynny. Gallwn i fod wedi marw erbyn hyn. Beth ydych chi'n ei wneud mewn gwirionedd, a beth allwch chi ei wneud i'm hetholwr, fel y gall ddisgwyl yn realistig cael yr apwyntiad a'r driniaeth y mae wedi bod yn aros mor hir amdanyn nhw? Diolch.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: I'm grateful for the question. I would respectfully ask the Member to reflect on the code of conduct on pursuing our own particular cases within the Welsh Parliament. But, of course, it is right that we all represent people who have been waiting a very long time on waiting lists. It is the length of waiting lists in terms of numbers and it is the length of time that people are waiting on them that have led this Government to conclude, even before we came into Government, that this was a priority. It's why we prioritised in the last budget, for 2026-27, the need to invest in the NHS now. It's why decisions have been made through the supplementary budget, which we hope can be passed today, in order to spend on bringing down waiting times and making the system sustainable, because it is unacceptable. Wherever people are—and that, of course, includes people here in this Siambr who are on waiting lists—it's not acceptable that we believe this to be normal, and that is why we are placing the utmost seriousness on the work of working with health boards, making the investment, having those performance reviews so that we can build a sustainable NHS and care system for the future.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Rwy'n ddiolchgar am y cwestiwn. Byddwn yn gofyn â pharch i'r Aelod fyfyrio ar y cod ymddygiad ar fynd ar drywydd ein hachosion penodol ein hunain o fewn Senedd Cymru. Ond, wrth gwrs, mae'n iawn ein bod ni i gyd yn cynrychioli pobl sydd wedi bod yn aros amser maith iawn ar restrau aros. Hyd y rhestrau aros o ran niferoedd a hyd yr amser y mae pobl yn aros arnyn nhw sydd wedi arwain y Llywodraeth hon i ddod i'r casgliad, hyd yn oed cyn i ni ddod i mewn i Lywodraeth, bod hyn yn flaenoriaeth. Dyna pam y gwnaethom ni flaenoriaethu yn y gyllideb ddiwethaf, ar gyfer 2026-27, yr angen i fuddsoddi yn y GIG rŵan. Dyna pam mae penderfyniadau wedi cael eu gwneud drwy'r gyllideb atodol, yr ydym ni'n gobeithio y gellir ei phasio heddiw, er mwyn gwario ar leihau amseroedd aros a gwneud y system yn gynaliadwy, oherwydd mae'n annerbyniol. Ble bynnag y mae pobl—ac mae hynny, wrth gwrs, yn cynnwys pobl yma yn y Siambr hon sydd ar restrau aros—nid yw'n dderbyniol ein bod ni'n credu bod hyn yn normal, a dyna pam rydym ni'n neilltuo'r difrifoldeb mwyaf i'r gwaith o weithio gyda byrddau iechyd, gwneud y buddsoddiad, cynnal yr adolygiadau perfformiad hynny fel y gallwn ni adeiladu GIG a system ofal cynaliadwy ar gyfer y dyfodol.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Brif Weinidog, diolch. And as you've raised Standing Orders, I'm sure the Member who spoke was speaking on behalf of his constituents as well, whilst drawing on a personal experience. But, just to clarify, indeed, speaking on behalf of constituents is our imperative here. Carrie Harper.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Brif Weinidog, diolch. A chan eich bod chi wedi codi Rheolau Sefydlog, rwy'n siŵr bod yr Aelod a siaradodd yn siarad ar ran ei etholwyr hefyd, tra'n tynnu ar brofiad personol. Ond, dim ond i egluro, yn wir, siarad ar ran etholwyr yw ein gorchymyn yma. Carrie Harper.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch, Lywydd. The issue of parking at the Maelor hospital in Wrexham is raised with us time and time again, and some residents have told us that they've arrived sometimes up to three hours before an appointment just to find a parking space. And that will be contributing to the 27,000 missed appointments at the Maelor last year. We've raised that repeatedly with the health board, alongside other local Members as well, the council and residents, too, yet there are still no concrete plans to tackle the problem. My own mother is currently undergoing cancer treatment, so I've seen first-hand the extra stress that that causes for people who are already worried about their health. I welcome the Government's commitment in the supplementary budget to boost funding for the NHS, and I also hope that this budget passes to allow that support to happen. First Minister, do you agree that accessing healthcare should begin at the hospital entrance and not with a queue for a parking space? And what discussions is the Welsh Government having with Betsi Cadwaladr to ensure that this long-running problem is finally treated as a priority?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch, Lywydd. Mae mater parcio yn ysbyty Maelor yn Wrecsam yn cael ei godi gyda ni dro ar ôl tro, ac mae rhai trigolion wedi dweud wrthym ni eu bod nhw weithiau wedi cyrraedd hyd at dair awr cyn apwyntiad dim ond i ddod o hyd i le parcio. A bydd hynny'n cyfrannu at y 27,000 o apwyntiadau a fethwyd yn ysbyty Maelor y llynedd. Rydym ni wedi codi hynny dro ar ôl tro gyda'r bwrdd iechyd, ochr yn ochr ag Aelodau lleol eraill hefyd, y cyngor a thrigolion hefyd, ac eto nid oes unrhyw gynlluniau pendant i fynd i'r afael â'r broblem o hyd. Mae fy mam fy hun yn derbyn triniaeth ar gyfer canser ar hyn o bryd, felly rwyf i wedi gweld yn bersonol y straen ychwanegol y mae hynny'n ei achosi i bobl sydd eisoes yn poeni am eu hiechyd. Rwy'n croesawu ymrwymiad y Llywodraeth yn y gyllideb atodol i roi hwb i gyllid ar gyfer y GIG, ac rwy'n gobeithio hefyd y bydd y gyllideb hon yn pasio i ganiatáu i'r cymorth hwnnw ddigwydd. Brif Weinidog, a ydych chi'n cytuno y dylai cael mynediad at ofal iechyd ddechrau wrth fynedfa'r ysbyty ac nid gyda chiw am le parcio? A pha drafodaethau mae Llywodraeth Cymru yn eu cael gyda Betsi Cadwaladr i sicrhau bod y broblem hirhoedlog hon yn cael ei thrin fel blaenoriaeth o'r diwedd?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Well, I certainly agree that access to healthcare should not begin with anxiety about finding a parking space, and it is something that far too many people face. Betsi Cadwaladr University Health Board is responsible for the operation and management of parking across its estate. Welsh Government guidance sets out the principles and best practice that health boards should apply when managing car parking at hospital sites. The health board recognises the parking pressures at Wrexham Maelor Hospital in particular, and I understand that it's considering practical operational and management options to improve access for patients, visitors and staff, keeping emergency routes clear as well, which is very, very important. It's one of those elements on which my health Minister is eager to see improvement, wherever that might be in Wales.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Wel, rwy'n sicr yn cytuno na ddylai mynediad at ofal iechyd ddechrau gyda phryder am ddod o hyd i le parcio, ac mae'n rhywbeth y mae llawer gormod o bobl yn ei wynebu. Bwrdd Iechyd Prifysgol Betsi Cadwaladr sy'n gyfrifol am weithredu a rheoli trefniadau parcio ar draws ei ystad. Mae canllawiau Llywodraeth Cymru yn nodi'r egwyddorion a'r arferion gorau y dylai byrddau iechyd eu gweithredu wrth reoli trefniadau parcio ceir ar safleoedd ysbytai. Mae'r bwrdd iechyd yn cydnabod y pwysau parcio yn Ysbyty Maelor Wrecsam yn arbennig, ac rwy'n deall ei fod yn ystyried opsiynau gweithredu a rheoli ymarferol i wella mynediad i gleifion, ymwelwyr a staff, gan gadw llwybrau brys yn glir hefyd, sy'n bwysig iawn, iawn. Mae'n un o'r elfennau hynny lle mae fy Ngweinidog iechyd yn awyddus i weld gwelliant, ble bynnag y gallai hynny fod yng Nghymru.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: First Minister, Nigel Williams, the Member, was absolutely right to raise concerns about constituents waiting far too long for planned procedures, surgeries on waiting lists in Fflint Wrecsam. One particular area that I believe requires some extra focus, ironically, is that of cataract operations. People are having to wait two years or more for cataract operations. You'll appreciate, First Minister, during that time, that it can be debilitating for people, especially if they need to drive, in rural areas of my constituency of Fflint Wrecsam, when they're waiting for years for what is actually quite a simple procedure in the grand scheme of things. People who live just over the border in Cheshire are waiting six weeks for exactly the same operation to take place. It strikes me that there's an issue there with the commissioning of services, which could make a big difference to accelerating people's waits when it comes to cataract operations. So, would you look at that, First Minister, to see where, specifically, cataract operations can be accelerated to ensure that those thousands of people who are waiting currently no longer have to wait without being able to see properly?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Brif Weinidog, roedd Nigel Williams, yr Aelod, yn gwbl gywir i godi pryderon am etholwyr sy'n aros yn llawer rhy hir am driniaethau wedi'u cynllunio, llawdriniaethau ar restrau aros yn Fflint Wrecsam. Un maes penodol yr wyf i'n credu sydd angen ychydig o bwyslais ychwanegol, yn eironig, yw llawdriniaethau cataract. Mae pobl yn gorfod aros dwy flynedd neu fwy am lawdriniaethau cataract. Byddwch yn gwerthfawrogi, Brif Weinidog, yn ystod y cyfnod hwnnw, y gall fod yn wanychol i bobl, yn enwedig os oes angen iddyn nhw yrru, mewn ardaloedd gwledig o fy etholaeth i yn Fflint Wrecsam, pan fyddan nhw'n aros am flynyddoedd am yr hyn sydd mewn gwirionedd yn driniaeth eithaf syml o edrych ar bethau yn eu cyfanrwydd. Mae pobl sy'n byw yr ochr arall i'r ffin yn Swydd Gaer yn aros chwe wythnos i'r un llawdriniaeth yn union gael ei chyflawni. Mae'n fy nharo i fod problem yn hynny o beth gyda chomisiynu gwasanaethau, a allai wneud gwahaniaeth mawr i gyflymu arosiadau pobl o ran llawdriniaethau cataract. Felly, a wnewch chi edrych ar hynny, Brif Weinidog, i weld ble, yn benodol, y gellir cyflymu llawdriniaethau cataract i sicrhau nad oes yn rhaid i'r miloedd hynny o bobl sy'n aros ar hyn o bryd aros heb allu gweld yn iawn mwyach?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: As the Minister points out, that is something that the Government is doing. We know that, when it comes to the eyes, it is particularly important to pursue treatment as quickly as possible. It was one of those elements during COVID, I remember, when people were facing delays in accessing care because of COVID restrictions, and that was putting eyesight at risk. It's something that the Government is very, very aware of. It's one of those areas that's very much in mind when we look forward to continuing the performance review and putting in that sustainability, which will help across the NHS in time.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Fel y mae'r Gweinidog yn ei nodi, mae hynny'n rhywbeth y mae'r Llywodraeth yn ei wneud. Rydym ni'n gwybod, o ran y llygaid, ei bod hi'n arbennig o bwysig cael triniaeth cyn gynted â phosibl. Roedd yn un o'r elfennau hynny yn ystod COVID, rwy'n cofio, pan oedd pobl yn wynebu oedi cyn cael mynediad at ofal oherwydd cyfyngiadau COVID, ac roedd hynny'n peryglu golwg. Mae'n rhywbeth y mae'r Llywodraeth yn ymwybodol iawn, iawn ohono. Mae'n un o'r meysydd hynny sy'n sicr yn cael ei ystyried pan fyddwn ni'n edrych ymlaen at barhau â'r adolygiad perfformiad a chyflwyno'r cynaliadwyedd hwnnw, a fydd yn helpu ar draws y GIG ymhen amser.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Cwestiynau Heb Rybudd gan Arweinwyr y Pleidiau
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Questions Without Notice from the Party Leaders

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Galwaf yn awr ar arweinwyr y pleidiau i holi'r Prif Weinidog. Yn gyntaf, arweinydd Reform UK, Dan Thomas.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: I now call on the party leaders to question the First Minister. First, the leader of Reform UK, Dan Thomas.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Thank you, Llywydd. Continuing with the theme of the NHS, in this last week before recess I would like to get to the bottom of when two-year waits on the NHS will be eradicated, because thousands of people across Wales are still waiting, in pain and discomfort, for far too long. Now, during the election campaign, the First Minister said that two-year waits would be eradicated within a matter of months, and then his new health Minister said that they would be eradicated by the end of the four-year term. I then asked the First Minister who was right and, in a very long-winded answer, he said that he was. But then, just a couple of weeks ago, his finance Minister, on BBC Walescast, said that two-year waits would be gone in 12 months, so, in other words, a year. Now, a year is a lot longer than a matter of months. So, can the First Minister finally give us some more detail: by which month will two-year waits be finally eradicated in Wales, as they are in England?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch, Lywydd. Gan barhau â thema'r GIG, yn yr wythnos olaf hon cyn y toriad hoffwn geisio darganfod pryd y bydd arosiadau o ddwy flynedd ar y GIG yn cael eu dileu, oherwydd mae miloedd o bobl ledled Cymru yn dal i aros, mewn poen ac anghysur, am lawer rhy hir. Nawr, yn ystod yr ymgyrch etholiadol, dywedodd y Prif Weinidog y byddai arosiadau o ddwy flynedd yn cael eu dileu o fewn mater o fisoedd, ac yna dywedodd ei Weinidog iechyd newydd y bydden nhw'n cael eu dileu erbyn diwedd y tymor pedair blynedd. Gofynnais wedyn i'r Prif Weinidog pwy oedd yn iawn ac, mewn ateb hirwyntog iawn, dywedodd mai ef oedd yn iawn. Ond yna, dim ond wythnos neu ddwy yn ôl, dywedodd ei Weinidog cyllid, ar BBC Walescast, y byddai arosiadau o ddwy flynedd yn diflannu ymhen 12 mis, felly, mewn geiriau eraill, blwyddyn. Nawr, mae blwyddyn yn llawer hirach na mater o fisoedd. Felly, a all y Prif Weinidog roi mwy o fanylion i ni o'r diwedd: erbyn pa fis y bydd arosiadau o ddwy flynedd yn cael eu dileu o'r diwedd yng Nghymru, fel y maen nhw wedi cael eu dileu yn Lloegr?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: We could have a philosophical debate here about how many months is months. All I can say is that all the actions that have been taken by this Government within the first 100 days—. You know, commissioning that work on establishing the surgery hubs, on making sure that we put that investment through this supplementary budget that we want to get passed today, so that we can, both in capital spend and in resource spend, make that investment to drive down those two-year waits—. The actions that Government is taking are aligned with bringing down those two-year waits as quickly as we can. We want to do it in months. I not so much stick to that—that is precisely what we set out to do before coming into Government, and what we are actively delivering now in Government.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Fe allem ni gael dadl athronyddol yma ynglŷn â faint o fisoedd yw misoedd. Y cwbl y gallaf i ei ddweud yw bod yr holl gamau y mae'r Llywodraeth hon wedi eu cymryd yn ystod y 100 diwrnod cyntaf—. Wyddoch chi, comisiynu'r gwaith hwnnw ar sefydlu'r canolfannau llawfeddygaeth, ar wneud yn siŵr ein bod ni'n rhoi'r buddsoddiad hwnnw drwy'r gyllideb atodol hon yr ydym ni eisiau iddi gael ei phasio heddiw, fel y gallwn ni, o ran gwariant cyfalaf a gwariant adnoddau, wneud y buddsoddiad hwnnw i leihau'r arosiadau hynny o ddwy flynedd—. Mae'r camau y mae'r Llywodraeth yn eu cymryd yn cyd-fynd â lleihau'r arosiadau hynny o ddwy flynedd cyn gynted ag y gallwn ni. Rydym ni eisiau gwneud hynny mewn misoedd. Nid wyf i'n cadw cymaint at hynny—dyna'n union yr hyn yr oeddem ni'n bwriadu ei wneud cyn dod i mewn i Lywodraeth, a'r hyn yr ydym ni'n ei gyflawni'n weithredol rŵan mewn Llywodraeth.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
The First Minister gave a promise during the election that two-year waits would be eradicated within a matter of months. That clearly is not happening. These promises are coming back to haunt you. It was obviously a promise that was made in the heat of an election debate, just as were your comments about a road solution for the M4. Your Ministers keep punishing you for your off-the-cuff remarks by rowing back on the promises that you're making in the heat of debates.

Now, it is quite clear that the First Minister doesn't do the detail. There's no detail on two-year waits. There's no detail on tackling M4 congestion. There's no detail yet on childcare plans. You had 30 years to wait for this moment, and there's not even any detail on what Plaid's definition of a woman is. So, let's try an easy question, because we know this figure is somewhere in Plaid Cymru HQ: what are the initial costings of Plaid Cymru's childcare offer?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Gwnaeth y Prif Weinidog addewid yn ystod yr etholiad y byddai arosiadau o ddwy flynedd yn cael eu dileu o fewn mater o fisoedd. Mae'n amlwg nad yw hynny'n digwydd. Mae'r addewidion hyn yn dod yn ôl i'ch poenydio. Roedd yn amlwg yn addewid a wnaed ym mwrlwm dadl etholiadol, yn union fel eich sylwadau am ateb ffordd ar gyfer yr M4. Mae eich Gweinidogion yn parhau i'ch cosbi am eich sylwadau byrfyfyr trwy gefnu ar yr addewidion yr ydych chi'n eu gwneud ym mwrlwm dadleuon.

Nawr, mae'n eithaf amlwg nad yw'r Prif Weinidog yn un am fanylion. Nid oes unrhyw fanylion ar arosiadau o ddwy flynedd. Nid oes unrhyw fanylion ar fynd i'r afael â thagfeydd ar yr M4. Nid oes unrhyw fanylion eto ar gynlluniau gofal plant. Roedd gennych chi 30 mlynedd i aros am y foment hon, ac nid oes hyd yn oed unrhyw fanylion ar beth yw diffiniad Plaid Cymru o fenyw. Felly, gadewch i ni roi cynnig ar gwestiwn hawdd, gan ein bod ni'n gwybod bod y ffigur hwn rhywle ym mhencadlys Plaid Cymru: beth yw costiadau cychwynnol cynnig gofal plant Plaid Cymru?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
I mean, the costings around the childcare offer have been made public, and they are very much a part of the supplementary budget that is due to be voted on today. The childcare offer is made up of a specific fund of £55 million that is going to be partly in capital, partly in resource, to make sure that we're able to deliver, as the first phase of the roll-out of costed childcare, the completion of the 12.5 hours for two-year-olds. Now, that is what is being done. I literally cannot give you more detail than that. It's the money, it's the timescale, and it's going to be done within this financial year.

Now, I know the Member couldn't decide which question to ask today, so he tried to bring eight into one. But in terms of accusing me of giving an off-the-cuff reply on the M4, it was an off-the-cuff reply based on 15 years of Plaid Cymru policy that we want to see a solution to the problems on the M4 in the Newport area—work that has already begun under my Deputy Minister for Transport and that we will be reporting on in the autumn of this year.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Hynny yw, mae'r costiadau ynghylch y cynnig gofal plant wedi cael eu cyhoeddi, ac maen nhw'n sicr yn rhan o'r gyllideb atodol y bydd pleidlais arni heddiw. Mae'r cynnig gofal plant wedi'i gyfansoddi o gronfa benodol o £55 miliwn sy'n mynd i fod yn rhannol mewn cyfalaf, yn rhannol mewn adnoddau, i wneud yn siŵr ein bod ni'n gallu sicrhau, fel cam cyntaf cyflwyno gofal plant wedi'i gostio, cwblhau'r 12.5 awr ar gyfer plant dwy oed. Rŵan, dyna beth sy'n cael ei wneud. Ni allaf i'n llythrennol roi mwy o fanylion i chi na hynny. Dyna'r arian, dyna'r amserlen, ac mae'n mynd i gael ei wneud yn ystod y flwyddyn ariannol hon.

Rŵan, rwy'n gwybod na allai'r Aelod benderfynu pa gwestiwn i'w ofyn heddiw, felly ceisiodd ddod ag wyth i mewn i un. Ond o ran fy nghyhuddo i o roi ateb byrfyfyr ar yr M4, roedd yn ateb byrfyfyr wedi'i seilio ar 15 mlynedd o bolisi Plaid Cymru ein bod ni eisiau gweld ateb i'r problemau ar yr M4 yn ardal Casnewydd—gwaith sydd eisoes wedi dechrau o dan fy Nirprwy Weinidog Trafnidiaeth ac y byddwn ni'n adrodd arno yn ystod yr hydref eleni.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Fifteen years, and all your transport Minister could come up with is closing junctions. Now, one way to stop congestion is to stop cars getting onto the M4. I'll give you that, but the people of Newport will not be very happy with that.

I asked for initial costings. Costings for phase 1 is not the initial costings. You said during the election campaign your promises were fully costed. Then you're downgrading them to initial costings. Then you're downgrading it to costings for phase 1. So, you clearly haven't got a plan. And if we do get those costings within the first 100 days, the 100 days ends during recess. So, we can't scrutinise when you actually issue those, but we will be here in September, waiting to scrutinise those figures.

But, First Minister, if your supplementary budget is voted down today, are you prepared to come back during the summer recess with a revised budget, or is this a part-time Plaid Government? Or are you content for the plans within your supplementary budget to languish for months upon months because you're too stubborn to do a deal?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Pymtheg mlynedd, a'r cwbl allai eich Gweinidog trafnidiaeth feddwl amdano yw cau cyffyrdd. Nawr, un ffordd o atal tagfeydd yw atal ceir rhag mynd ar yr M4. Fe wnaf i gytuno â chi am hynny, ond ni fydd pobl Casnewydd yn hapus iawn gyda hynny.

Gofynnais am gostiadau cychwynnol. Nid costiadau ar gyfer cam 1 yw'r costiadau cychwynnol. Fe wnaethoch chi ddweud yn ystod yr ymgyrch etholiadol bod eich addewidion wedi'u costio'n llawn. Yna rydych chi'n eu hisraddio i gostiadau cychwynnol. Yna rydych chi'n ei israddio i gostiadau ar gyfer cam 1. Felly, mae'n amlwg nad oes gennych chi gynllun. Ac os ydym ni'n cael y costiadau hynny yn ystod y 100 diwrnod cyntaf, mae'r 100 diwrnod yn dod i ben yn ystod y toriad. Felly, allwn ni ddim craffu pan fyddwch chi'n cyhoeddi'r rheini mewn gwirionedd, ond byddwn ni yma ym mis Medi, yn aros i graffu ar y ffigurau hynny.

Ond, Brif Weinidog, os bydd eich cyllideb atodol yn colli'r bleidlais heddiw, a ydych chi'n barod i ddychwelyd yn ystod toriad yr haf gyda chyllideb ddiwygiedig, neu ai Llywodraeth Plaid Cymru ran-amser yw hon? Neu a ydych chi'n fodlon i'r cynlluniau yn eich cyllideb atodol gael eu hesgeuluso am fisoedd ar fisoedd oherwydd eich bod chi'n rhy ystyfnig i daro bargen?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: [Inaudible.]—the idea that, from opposition, we were unable to resolve the problems of the M4—. We were in opposition over those years. He was in the Conservative Party, so I get the confusion there about where his politics land. Listen, I understand that there is frustration in wanting a holiday after eight weeks of being the leader of Reform in here. We will be working through the last 43 days of the 100-day plan, every single day of that reporting on it as we promised the people of Wales we would, and then cracking on with phase 2, which is that programme for government to transform the lives of the people of Wales. But today we need to get a supplementary budget through, to get working on the NHS, on childcare, on additional learning needs and all those issues that matter to the people of Wales.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: [Anghlywadwy.]—y syniad nad oeddem ni, o fod yn wrthblaid, yn gallu datrys problemau'r M4—. Roeddem ni'n wrthwynebiad yn ystod y blynyddoedd hynny. Roedd ef yn y Blaid Geidwadol, felly rwy'n deall y dryswch yn y fan honno ynglŷn â ble mae ei wleidyddiaeth yn glanio. Gwrandewch, rwy'n deall bod rhwystredigaeth o ran bod eisiau gwyliau ar ôl wyth wythnos o fod yn arweinydd Reform yma. Byddwn yn gweithio trwy 43 diwrnod olaf y cynllun 100 diwrnod, bob un diwrnod o hwnnw yn adrodd arno fel y gwnaethom ni addo i bobl Cymru y byddem ni'n ei wneud, ac yna'n bwrw ymlaen â cham 2, sef y rhaglen lywodraeth honno i drawsnewid bywydau pobl Cymru. Ond heddiw mae angen i ni gael cyllideb atodol drwodd, i ddechrau gweithio ar y GIG, ar ofal plant, ar anghenion dysgu ychwanegol a'r holl faterion hynny sy'n bwysig i bobl Cymru.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Arweinydd Llafur Cymru, Ken Skates.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: The leader of Welsh Labour, Ken Skates.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch. First Minister, over the past few days, a crisis developed, the like of which I fear we will see again and again. Homes were evacuated, schools were closed, hundreds of acres of land were scorched and businesses hit during the north Wales wildfires and extreme heat. Now, thanks to our emergency services, the loss of human life was averted. First Minister, who is responsible in your Government for responding to such events?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch. Brif Weinidog, dros y dyddiau diwethaf, datblygodd argyfwng, o'r math yr wyf i'n ofni y byddwn ni'n ei weld dro ar ôl tro. Cafodd cartrefi eu gwagio, ysgolion eu cau, llosgwyd cannoedd o erwau o dir a tharwyd busnesau yn ystod tanau gwyllt a gwres eithafol gogledd Cymru. Nawr, diolch i'n gwasanaethau brys, llwyddwyd i osgoi colli bywydau dynol. Brif Weinidog, pwy sy'n gyfrifol yn eich Llywodraeth am ymateb i ddigwyddiadau o'r fath?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: This is a cross-government response, of course. We have Ministers directly involved in working with the particular emergency services, of course. But this is a cross-government approach, in that these fires may have started yesterday, but they are caused by man-made climate change that all of us across Government are committed to addressing.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Mae hwn yn ymateb traws-lywodraethol, wrth gwrs. Mae gennym ni Weinidogion sy'n ymwneud yn uniongyrchol â gweithio gyda'r gwasanaethau brys penodol, wrth gwrs. Ond mae hwn yn ddull traws-lywodraethol, oherwydd efallai fod y tanau hyn wedi dechrau ddoe, ond maen nhw'n cael eu hachosi gan newid hinsawdd a achoswyd gan bobl y mae pob un ohonom ni ar draws y Llywodraeth wedi ymrwymo i fynd i'r afael ag ef.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Thank you, First Minister. Of course, the risk with it being cross-government is that no single Minister actually holds on to the responsibility. Now, that was the distinct advantage of having a Minister for north Wales. This week, the Welsh Government has been pretty much silent in north Wales and about north Wales whilst these fires have taken place. More people may be left homeless in weeks and months to come with further extreme heat predicted, and that means that businesses will also be hit, likely events will be cancelled. Can you assure people across Wales that your Government will support businesses and home owners who are impacted by wildfires and extreme heat?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch, Brif Weinidog. Wrth gwrs, y perygl gyda'r ffaith ei fod yn draws-lywodraeth yw nad oes unrhyw Weinidog unigol yn meddu ar y cyfrifoldeb. Nawr, dyna oedd y fantais amlwg o fod â Gweinidog dros ogledd Cymru. Yr wythnos hon, mae Llywodraeth Cymru wedi bod fwy neu lai'n fud yng ngogledd Cymru ac am ogledd Cymru tra bod y tanau hyn wedi digwydd. Efallai y bydd mwy o bobl yn cael eu gadael yn ddigartref yn yr wythnosau a'r misoedd i ddod gyda gwres eithafol pellach yn cael ei ragweld, ac mae hynny'n golygu y bydd busnesau yn cael eu taro hefyd, mae'n debygol y bydd digwyddiadau yn cael eu canslo. A allwch chi sicrhau pobl ledled Cymru y bydd eich Llywodraeth yn cynorthwyo busnesau a pherchnogion tai sy'n cael eu heffeithio gan danau gwyllt a gwres eithafol?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Of course, my Government will do everything we can and already have done to support those who are affected by these fires. My thanks initially go to the people who responded to them. My thoughts are with the people who are affected by them.

On the question of a Minister for north Wales, I have a Minister for north Wales. It's Siân Gwenllian, and it's Dafydd Trystan, and it's Anna Brychan, it's Mabon ap Gwynfor, it's Sioned Williams—all my Ministers are Ministers for all of Wales. Where was Labour's Minister for the south of Wales, if that matters? Because all my Ministers are Ministers for the south of Wales too, and the west of Wales, and mid Wales, because we are a joined-up Government that has a plan for our nation—all of our nation.

That is why all of us have come together around this supplementary budget today—north, south, east, west, and mid, it's important to remember—with a determination to change the lives of the people of Wales for the better. We have a supplementary budget that is focused on making the NHS sustainable. I will be voting for that sustainability for the NHS. The leader of Labour in Wales is threatening to vote against that. I will be voting for expanding free school meals under this supplementary budget. The Labour leader here is threatening to vote against that. I will be voting for the expansion of paid-for childcare in Wales. The Labour leader threatens to vote against that. And, yes, I will be voting for a package worth £120 million for ALN that he and I negotiated positively on, and he is threatening to vote to not allow that spending to go ahead. This is a Government for all of Wales with a vision for all of our nation.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Wrth gwrs, bydd fy Llywodraeth yn gwneud popeth y gallwn ac rydym ni eisoes wedi gwneud hynny i gynorthwyo'r rhai sydd wedi'u heffeithio gan y tanau hyn. Mae fy niolch i ddechrau yn mynd i'r bobl a ymatebodd iddyn nhw. Mae fy meddyliau gyda'r bobl sy'n cael eu heffeithio ganddyn nhw.

Ar y cwestiwn o Weinidog dros ogledd Cymru, mae gen i Weinidog dros ogledd Cymru. Siân Gwenllian, a Dafydd Trystan, ac Anna Brychan, Mabon ap Gwynfor, Sioned Williams—mae fy holl Weinidogion yn Weinidogion dros Gymru gyfan. Ble oedd Gweinidog Llafur dros dde Cymru, os yw hynny'n bwysig? Oherwydd mae fy holl Weinidogion yn Weinidogion dros dde Cymru hefyd, a gorllewin Cymru, a chanolbarth Cymru, gan ein bod ni'n Llywodraeth gydgysylltiedig sydd â chynllun ar gyfer ein cenedl—ein cenedl gyfan.

Dyna pam mae pob un ohonom wedi dod at ein gilydd o amgylch y gyllideb atodol hon heddiw—gogledd, de, dwyrain, gorllewin, a chanolbarth, mae'n bwysig cofio—gyda phenderfyniad i newid bywydau pobl Cymru er gwell. Mae gennym ni gyllideb atodol sy'n canolbwyntio ar wneud y GIG yn gynaliadwy. Byddaf i'n pleidleisio dros y cynaliadwyedd hwnnw i'r GIG. Mae arweinydd Llafur yng Nghymru yn bygwth pleidleisio yn erbyn hynny. Byddaf i'n pleidleisio dros ehangu prydau ysgol am ddim o dan y gyllideb atodol hon. Mae'r arweinydd Llafur yma yn bygwth pleidleisio yn erbyn hynny. Byddaf i'n pleidleisio dros ehangu gofal plant y telir amdano yng Nghymru. Mae'r arweinydd Llafur yn bygwth pleidleisio yn erbyn hynny. A byddaf, byddaf i'n pleidleisio dros becyn gwerth £120 miliwn ar gyfer ADY y gwnaeth ef a minnau ei gytuno'n gadarnhaol, ac mae'n bygwth pleidleisio i beidio â chaniatáu i'r gwariant hwnnw ddigwydd. Mae hon yn Llywodraeth ar gyfer Cymru gyfan â gweledigaeth ar gyfer ein cenedl gyfan.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: The leader of the Welsh Conservatives, Darren Millar.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Diolch, Lywydd. If you'll indulge me, I'd like to pay tribute, on behalf of the Welsh Conservatives, to Bonnie Tyler. Tributes have poured in, of course, across Wales about the loss of this Welsh icon, a singer with global fame and impact, a unique artist with a unique voice, and we want to pay tribute to her and send our best wishes to her family and her loved ones. Of course, we're also in shock at the loss of Ann Widdecombe, a colourful political character, a precious character to people across the whole of the United Kingdom, but especially here in Wales for those who met her.

First Minister, thanks to the members of the public right across Wales, our country now recycles more household waste than anywhere else in the United Kingdom, and our glass recycling rate is amongst the highest in Europe. Yet, in spite of this, your Plaid Cymru Government wants to follow the previous Labour Government's plans to diverge from the rest of the United Kingdom and insist on including glass in its deposit-return scheme from October. We know it's going to push costs on to businesses, manufacturers and consumers. What assessment has your Government made of the additional costs of this scheme and what are you going to do to mitigate them?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch, Lywydd. Os gwnewch chi fy nghaniatáu, hoffwn dalu teyrnged, ar ran y Ceidwadwyr Cymreig, i Bonnie Tyler. Mae teyrngedau wedi llifo i mewn, wrth gwrs, ledled Cymru am golli'r eicon Cymreig hon, cantores sydd ag enwogrwydd ac effaith fyd-eang, artist unigryw â llais unigryw, ac rydym ni eisiau talu teyrnged iddi ac anfon ein dymuniadau gorau i'w theulu a'i hanwyliaid. Wrth gwrs, rydym ni hefyd mewn sioc o golli Ann Widdecombe, cymeriad gwleidyddol lliwgar, cymeriad gwerthfawr i bobl ar draws y Deyrnas Unedig gyfan, ond yn enwedig yma yng Nghymru i'r rhai a wnaeth ei chyfarfod.

Brif Weinidog, diolch i aelodau'r cyhoedd ledled Cymru, mae ein gwlad bellach yn ailgylchu mwy o wastraff cartref nag unrhyw le arall yn y Deyrnas Unedig, ac mae ein cyfradd ailgylchu gwydr ymhlith yr uchaf yn Ewrop. Ac eto, er gwaethaf hyn, mae eich Llywodraeth Plaid Cymru eisiau dilyn cynlluniau'r Llywodraeth Lafur flaenorol i wyro oddi wrth weddill y Deyrnas Unedig a mynnu ar gynnwys gwydr yn ei chynllun dychwelyd ernes o fis Hydref ymlaen. Rydym ni'n gwybod ei fod yn mynd i wthio costau ymlaen i fusnesau, gweithgynhyrchwyr a defnyddwyr. Pa asesiad mae eich Llywodraeth wedi ei wneud o gostau ychwanegol y cynllun hwn a beth ydych chi'n mynd i'w wneud i'w lliniaru?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
I will, of course, firstly, also send my condolences to the loved ones of Bonnie Tyler, a national treasure who was a part of my life as long as I care to remember. She will be fondly, fondly remembered by all of us here in Wales and far, far beyond. And, yes, Ann Widdecombe: we share in the grief of her loved ones, but also in the fear around the safety of politicians and public figures, and these are negotiations and discussions that we should all across this Chamber be eager to engage with in a non-party political way.

On the deposit-return scheme, I note that the Conservatives supported the DRS with glass. This is the starting point, and always at a time of difficulty in the implementation of a policy, it's important to remember where we came from. Why is it that the Conservatives said they supported including glass? Why is it that the last Senedd voted for the inclusion of glass, which is something that this Government is respecting in taking this matter forward? It is because it does go further than recycling. It is the reuse. It is about that environmental responsibility. It is about also being a trailblazer, because there's an agreement in principle in other parts of the UK to progressing with glass. We can be the ones showing the way.

Are there challenges? Yes, which is why exemptions have been made clear for small retailers, for small producers, for example. But given that it's the right thing to do, you don't always allow the fact that there are challenges—very real ones, absolutely—to stop you in your tracks when there's a prize worth aiming for.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Fe wnaf i, wrth gwrs, yn gyntaf, anfon fy nghydymdeimlad hefyd at anwyliaid Bonnie Tyler, trysor cenedlaethol a oedd yn rhan o fy mywyd cyn belled yn ôl ag y gallaf i gofio. Bydd yn cael ei chofio'n hoffus, hoffus iawn gan bob un ohonom ni yma yng Nghymru ac ymhell iawn y tu hwnt. Ac, ie, Ann Widdecombe: rydym ni'n rhannu yng ngalar ei hanwyliaid, ond hefyd yn yr ofn ynghylch diogelwch gwleidyddion a ffigyrau cyhoeddus, ac mae'r rhain yn drafodaethau y dylem ni i gyd ar draws y Siambr hon fod yn awyddus i gymryd rhan ynddyn nhw mewn ffordd nad yw'n wleidyddiaeth plaid.

Ar y cynllun dychwelyd ernes, rwy'n sylwi bod y Ceidwadwyr wedi cefnogi'r cynllun hwn gyda gwydr. Dyma'r man cychwyn, a bob amser ar adeg o anhawster wrth weithredu polisi, mae'n bwysig cofio o le daethom ni. Pam wnaeth y Ceidwadwyr ddweud eu bod nhw'n cefnogi cynnwys gwydr? Pam wnaeth y Senedd ddiwethaf bleidleisio o blaid cynnwys gwydr, sy'n rhywbeth y mae'r Llywodraeth hon yn ei barchu wrth fynd fwrw ymlaen â'r mater hwn? Mae oherwydd ei fod yn mynd ymhellach nag ailgylchu. Mae'n fater o ailddefnyddio. Mae'n ymwneud â'r cyfrifoldeb amgylcheddol hwnnw. Mae'n ymwneud â bod yn arloeswr hefyd, oherwydd ceir cytundeb mewn egwyddor mewn rhannau eraill o'r DU i symud ymlaen gyda gwydr. Fe allwn ni fod y rhai sy'n dangos y ffordd.

A oes heriau? Oes, a dyna pam mae eithriadau wedi cael eu gwneud yn eglur i fanwerthwyr bach, i gynhyrchwyr bach, er enghraifft. Ond o gofio mai dyma'r peth iawn i'w wneud, nid ydych bob amser yn caniatáu i'r ffaith bod heriau—rhai real iawn, yn sicr—eich stopio yn stond pan fo gwobr sy'n werth anelu amdani.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Look, First Minister, we all agree that we need to get to grips with litter and improve even further our recycling rates, but we've already got a by-election this summer with a man dressed up as a bin; the last thing we need is another row about rubbish receptacles, if I can put it that way, here in Wales. Now, councils are actually cutting litter bins across the country because they can’t afford to provide them and can't afford to empty them. Fly-tipping is on the up. Ninety per cent of glass is already recycled in Wales because of the kerbside recycling system and the engagement of the public with it. Why does your Government think it's acceptable to impose extra costs on small shopkeepers and force householders to face the inconvenience of having to drive with their cars full of bottles back to the shops, rather than simply leaving those glass bottles at the kerbside for collection and recycling? Why don't you make it simple for manufacturers, simple for retailers and simple for the public and bin this unnecessary policy?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Edrychwch, Brif Weinidog, rydym ni i gyd yn cytuno bod angen i ni fynd i'r afael â sbwriel a gwella ein cyfraddau ailgylchu hyd yn oed ymhellach, ond mae gennym ni isetholiad yr haf hwn eisoes â dyn wedi gwisgo fel bin; y peth olaf sydd ei angen arnom ni yw ffrae arall am gynwysyddion sbwriel, os caf i ei roi felly, yma yng Nghymru. Nawr, mae cynghorau mewn gwirionedd yn lleihau nifer y biniau sbwriel ledled y wlad gan nad ydyn nhw'n gallu fforddio eu darparu nhw ac ni allan nhw fforddio eu gwagio. Mae tipio anghyfreithlon ar gynnydd. Mae naw deg y cant o wydr eisoes yn cael ei ailgylchu yng Nghymru oherwydd y system ailgylchu ar garreg y drws ac ymgysylltiad y cyhoedd â hi. Pam mae eich Llywodraeth yn meddwl ei bod yn dderbyniol gorfodi costau ychwanegol ar siopwyr bach a gorfodi deiliaid tai i wynebu'r anghyfleustra o orfod gyrru gyda'u ceir yn llawn poteli yn ôl i'r siopau, yn hytrach na gadael y poteli gwydr hynny ar garreg y drws i gael eu casglu a'u hailgylchu? Pam na wnewch chi hi'n syml i weithgynhyrchwyr, yn syml i fanwerthwyr ac yn syml i'r cyhoedd a chael gwared ar y polisi diangen hwn?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Bins being a theme here, I like the rubbish receptacle trashing, of course, the reputation of the leader of Reform currently. Again, when you're talking about people driving places to get rid of bottles, at the core of DRS, as a principle, is people taking things places, so that doesn't make a difference whether it's plastic or glass, and the Member does agree that it's the right thing to ask people to take those plastic bottles somewhere in order to deal with that problem of plastic. I understand that there are challenges, and I know that my Minister is dealing with those challenges now, and putting the practical measures in place in order to deliver this. What we're saying is that we believe that this can be overcome. The Member mentions the additional cost to small retailers. There is an exemption for small retailers who don't have that square footage, that space to put the machines in and so on. These are things that the Government is taking into consideration, but we believe that this is doable, and we do not believe the threats of the very large manufacturers of extremely large increases in prices. The sums don't add up.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Gan fod biniau yn thema yma, rwy'n hoffi'r cynhwysydd sbwriel yn taflu, wrth gwrs, enw da arweinydd Reform ar y domen ar hyn o bryd. Eto, pan fyddwch chi'n sôn am bobl yn gyrru i leoedd i gael gwared ar boteli, wrth wraidd y cynllun dychwelyd ernes, fel egwyddor, y mae pobl yn mynd â phethau i leoedd, felly nid yw hynny'n gwneud gwahaniaeth pa un a yw'n blastig neu'n wydr, ac mae'r Aelod yn cytuno mai'r peth iawn i'w wneud yw gofyn i bobl fynd â'r poteli plastig hynny i rywle er mwyn delio â'r broblem honno o blastig. Rwy'n deall bod heriau, ac rwy'n gwybod bod fy Ngweinidog yn delio â'r heriau hynny rŵan, ac yn rhoi'r mesurau ymarferol ar waith er mwyn cyflawni hyn. Yr hyn yr ydym ni'n ei ddweud yw ein bod ni'n credu y gellir goresgyn hyn. Mae'r Aelod yn sôn am y gost ychwanegol i fanwerthwyr bach. Ceir eithriad i fanwerthwyr bach nad yw'r troedfeddi sgwâr hynny ganddyn nhw, y lle hwnnw i roi'r peiriannau i mewn ac yn y blaen. Mae'r rhain yn bethau y mae'r Llywodraeth yn eu cymryd i ystyriaeth, ond rydym ni'n credu fod hyn yn bosibl, ac nid ydym ni'n credu bygythiadau'r gweithgynhyrchwyr mawr iawn o gynnydd eithriadol o fawr i brisiau. Nid yw'r symiau'n gwneud synnwyr.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
