XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Defence Investment Plan

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: 3. Pa ddadansoddiad y mae'r Llywodraeth wedi ei wneud o effaith cynllun gwariant ar amddiffyn Llywodraeth y DU ar gyllideb cyfalaf Llywodraeth Cymru? OQ64409
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: 3. What analysis has the Government made of the impact of the UK Government's defence investment plan on the Welsh Government's capital budget? OQ64409

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Mi ydyn ni’n amcangyfrif y bydd gostyngiad o £25 miliwn i £30 miliwn o leiaf yng nghyllideb gyfalaf Llywodraeth Cymru yn y flwyddyn ariannol hon, efo gostyngiadau pellach yn y blynyddoedd i ddod. Mae Llywodraeth y Deyrnas Gyfunol hefyd wedi nodi y bydd angen dod o hyd i £4.7 biliwn ychwanegol yng nghyllideb yr hydref. Felly, dyma’r gostyngiad lleiaf y gallwn ei ddisgwyl, ac mi allai fod yn fwy. Mi fydd hyn yn cael effaith uniongyrchol ar ein hysgolion, ein hysbytai a’n cysylltedd trafnidiaeth.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: We estimate that there will be a reduction of £25 million to £30 million at least in the Welsh Government's capital budget in the current financial year, with further reductions in future years. The UK Government has also indicated that there will be a need to find a further £4.7 billion in the autumn budget. So, this is the minimum cut that we could expect, and it could be larger. This will have a direct impact on our schools, our hospitals and our transport connectivity.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Prif Weinidog, we can all see that the threats to national security are numerous, but it can't be right that Wales will be denied years of capital funding to cover the failure of consecutive UK Governments to give us an armed forces fit for the future. Once again, the needs of Wales have been, at best, an afterthought. Thirty one of 32 schools in Torfaen require urgent maintenance, and there's a £5 million backlog for repairs in Monmouthshire schools. The money we will lose will directly affect areas like mine, and this means that issues that need to be addressed urgently will have to be pushed back. So, bearing this in mind, how will the First Minister keep making the case to the UK Government to redress this? Diolch.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Brif Weinidog, rydym ni i gyd yn gallu gweld bod y bygythiadau i ddiogelwch cenedlaethol yn niferus, ond ni all fod yn iawn y bydd Cymru yn cael gwrthod blynyddoedd o gyllid cyfalaf i wneud iawn am fethiant Llywodraethau'r DU yn olynol i roi lluoedd arfog sy'n addas ar gyfer y dyfodol i ni. Unwaith eto, mae anghenion Cymru, ar yr ochr orau, wedi bod yn ôl-ystyriaeth. Mae angen gwaith cynnal a chadw brys yn un ar hugain o 32 o ysgolion yn Nhorfaen, a cheir ôl-groniad o £5 miliwn ar gyfer atgyweiriadau yn ysgolion sir Fynwy. Bydd yr arian y byddwn ni'n ei golli yn effeithio'n uniongyrchol ar ardaloedd fel fy un i, ac mae hyn yn golygu y bydd yn rhaid gwthio materion y mae angen mynd i'r afael â nhw ar frys yn ôl. Felly, o gofio hyn, sut wnaiff y Prif Weinidog barhau i wneud y ddadl i Lywodraeth y DU unioni hyn? Diolch.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: It is a very important point. We absolutely recognise the changing face of the threats that we face currently and the arguments in favour of strengthening defence spending, including in the cyber sector, in which we have real expertise here in Wales, but Wales should not be peculiarly disadvantaged by the way the UK Government has gone about with its decisions on defence spending. Departments in the UK Government in Whitehall would have been able to make the case for protecting budgets. The handing down in this way without negotiation with Wales of ongoing cuts to capital, which were under severe strain anyway, will inevitably mean needing to cut back on spending on health and education. The first supplementary budget allocates £40 million of additional capital funding this year to support the urgent maintenance and repair works across schools, the kind of which the Members mentions. That is put under threat. But, of course, we need to get the supplementary budget through first in order to make that spending.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Mae'n bwynt pwysig iawn. Rydym ni'n cydnabod yn llwyr wyneb newidiol y bygythiadau sy'n ein hwynebu ar hyn o bryd a'r dadleuon o blaid cryfhau gwariant ar amddiffyn, gan gynnwys yn y sector seiber, lle mae gennym ni arbenigedd gwirioneddol yma yng Nghymru, ond ni ddylai Cymru fod dan anfantais arbennig gan y ffordd y mae Llywodraeth y DU wedi mynd ati i wneud ei phenderfyniadau am wariant ar amddiffyn. Byddai adrannau yn Llywodraeth y DU yn Whitehall wedi gallu gwneud y ddadl dros ddiogelu cyllidebau. Bydd trosglwyddo toriadau parhaus i gyfalaf, a oedd dan straen difrifol beth bynnag, yn y modd hwn heb drafodaeth â Chymru, yn golygu yn anochel bod angen lleihau gwariant ar iechyd ac addysg. Mae'r gyllideb atodol gyntaf yn dyrannu £40 miliwn o gyllid cyfalaf ychwanegol eleni i gynorthwyo'r gwaith cynnal a chadw ac atgyweirio brys ar draws ysgolion, o'r math y mae'r Aelodau yn sôn amdano. Mae hynny'n cael ei roi dan fygythiad. Ond, wrth gwrs, mae angen i ni gael y gyllideb atodol drwodd yn gyntaf er mwyn gwneud y gwariant hwnnw.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: First Minister, Reform UK makes no apology for supporting increased investment in Britain's armed forces at a time of growing global instability. National defence is the first duty of any Government, so, rather than blaming Westminster for difficult spending decisions, will you explain what efficiencies the Welsh Government is prepared to make within its own capital programme before claiming Wales cannot cope? How much money could be redirected by cancelling lower priority projects and reducing waste, so that essential infrastructure, such as roads, hospitals and schools, is protected while the UK strengthens our national security?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Brif Weinidog, nid yw Reform UK yn gwneud unrhyw ymddiheuriad am gefnogi mwy o fuddsoddiad yn lluoedd arfog Prydain ar adeg o ansefydlogrwydd byd-eang cynyddol. Amddiffyn cenedlaethol yw dyletswydd gyntaf unrhyw Lywodraeth, felly, yn hytrach na rhoi'r bai ar San Steffan am benderfyniadau gwariant anodd, a wnewch chi egluro pa arbedion effeithlonrwydd y mae Llywodraeth Cymru yn barod i'w gwneud yn ei rhaglen gyfalaf ei hun cyn honni na all Cymru ymdopi? Faint o arian ellid ei ailgyfeirio trwy ganslo prosiectau blaenoriaeth is a lleihau gwastraff, fel bod seilwaith hanfodol, fel ffyrdd, ysbytai ac ysgolion, yn cael ei ddiogelu tra bod y DU yn cryfhau ein diogelwch cenedlaethol?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: I would hope that all of us want to see capital spend on schools and hospitals. These are really, really important elements for the future of our nation. As I said, the point here is that we haven't been engaged in any of this discussion that ends up in cuts being made that will inevitably lead to cuts in public service capital spend. I have written to the Secretary of State for Wales, and the Cabinet Minister for Finance has written to the Chief Secretary of the Treasury, to raise those concerns, seek clarity of the impacts for our funding. As I say, it's completely unacceptable that Welsh capital budgets are impacted in this way. That does not take away from recognising the changing face of the threats that exist in the world around us, which are undeniable.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Byddwn yn gobeithio bod pob un ohonom ni eisiau gweld gwariant cyfalaf ar ysgolion ac ysbytai. Mae'r rhain yn elfennau pwysig dros ben ar gyfer dyfodol ein cenedl. Fel y dywedais i, y pwynt yma yw nad ydym ni wedi bod yn rhan o unrhyw ran o'r drafodaeth hon sy'n arwain at wneud toriadau a fydd yn arwain yn anochel at doriadau i wariant cyfalaf gwasanaethau cyhoeddus. Rwyf i wedi ysgrifennu at Ysgrifennydd Gwladol Cymru, ac mae'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyllid wedi ysgrifennu at Brif Ysgrifennydd y Trysorlys, i godi'r pryderon hynny, i ofyn am eglurder ynghylch yr effeithiau ar ein cyllid. Fel y dywedais i, mae'n gwbl annerbyniol bod cyllidebau cyfalaf Cymru yn cael eu heffeithio fel hyn. Nid yw hynny'n tynnu oddi wrth gydnabod wyneb newidiol y bygythiadau sy'n bodoli yn y byd o'n cwmpas, sy'n ddiamheuol.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: First Minister, rather than solely focusing on the impact to the Welsh Government's budget, what is the Government actually doing to maximise the opportunities of the defence investment plan that it can present to employers such as BAE Systems in Glascoed in my constituency and the wider defence sector? There are over 285 defence companies in Wales, contributing a £1 billion to our economy. Surely we should be focusing on what we can make out of this, instead of just bemoaning the situation.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Brif Weinidog, yn hytrach na chanolbwyntio ar yr effaith ar gyllideb Llywodraeth Cymru yn unig, beth mae'r Llywodraeth yn ei wneud mewn gwirionedd i sicrhau'r cyfleoedd mwyaf posibl o'r cynllun buddsoddi mewn amddiffyn y gall ei gyflwyno i gyflogwyr fel BAE Systems yn Glasgoed yn fy etholaeth i a'r sector amddiffyn ehangach? Ceir dros 285 o gwmnïau amddiffyn yng Nghymru, sy'n cyfrannu £1 biliwn at ein heconomi. Siawns y dylem ni fod yn canolbwyntio ar yr hyn y gallwn ei wneud allan o hyn, yn hytrach na dim ond achwyn am y sefyllfa.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: It's a separate question, but it's a very, very valid question: how, when defence spending is made, or when defence investment is made, there is at least equity in the way that that spend is made. If you look at the way UK Government distributes that investment, Wales has not been getting its share. If you look at the proportion of defence spend going to the south west of England, for example, compared with Wales, there is no comparison. So, the Member is right that there is an economic element to this, and that is something that we would look at in economic terms, and, of course, seeking opportunities for businesses involved in the ethical defence sector in Wales. But that does not mean that we should withdraw our concerns around how decisions are made that affect all of our constituencies, be it schools or hospitals and so on.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Mae'n gwestiwn ar wahân, ond mae'n gwestiwn dilys iawn, iawn: sut, pan fydd gwariant amddiffyn yn cael ei wneud, neu pan fydd buddsoddiad mewn amddiffyn yn cael ei wneud, bod tegwch yn y ffordd y mae'r gwariant hwnnw'n cael ei wneud o leiaf. Os edrychwch chi ar y ffordd y mae Llywodraeth y DU yn dosbarthu'r buddsoddiad hwnnw, nid yw Cymru wedi bod yn cael ei chyfran. Os edrychwch chi ar y gyfran o wariant amddiffyn sy'n mynd i dde-orllewin Lloegr, er enghraifft, o'i gymharu â Chymru, does dim cymhariaeth. Felly, mae'r Aelod yn iawn bod elfen economaidd i hyn, ac mae hynny'n rhywbeth y byddem ni'n ei ystyried o safbwynt economaidd, ac, wrth gwrs, yn chwilio am gyfleoedd i fusnesau sy'n ymwneud â'r sector amddiffyn moesegol yng Nghymru. Ond nid yw hynny'n golygu y dylem ni dynnu ein pryderon ynglŷn â sut mae penderfyniadau yn cael eu gwneud sy'n effeithio ar bob un o'n hetholaethau, boed yn ysgolion neu'n ysbytai ac yn y blaen.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Hyrwyddo Cydraddoldeb
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Promoting Equality

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: 4. A wnaiff y Prif Weinidog roi diweddariad ar yr hyn y mae Llywodraeth Cymru yn ei wneud i hyrwyddo cydraddoldeb yng Nghymru? OQ64429
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: 4. Will the First Minister provide an update on what the Welsh Government is doing to promote equality in Wales? OQ64429

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: In her oral statement of the 9 June, the Deputy First Minister and Cabinet Minister for Social Justice and Equality set out our priorities for promoting social justice: fostering respect, solidarity and fairness. We're committed to addressing inequalities in Wales. This includes supporting the delivery of the 'Anti-racist Wales Action Plan', disabled persons' rights plan and delivering on the British Sign Language (Wales) Act 2026.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Yn ei datganiad llafar ar 9 Mehefin, cyflwynodd y Dirprwy Brif Weinidog a'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyfiawnder Cymdeithasol a Chydraddoldeb ein blaenoriaethau ar gyfer hyrwyddo cyfiawnder cymdeithasol: meithrin parch, undod a thegwch. Rydym ni wedi ymrwymo i fynd i'r afael ag anghydraddoldebau yng Nghymru. Mae hyn yn cynnwys cefnogi darpariaeth 'Cynllun Gweithredu Gwrth-hiliaeth Cymru', cynllun hawliau pobl anabl a chyflawni o ran Deddf Iaith Arwyddion Prydain (Cymru) 2026.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: First Minister, the Welsh Government has a target whereby 20 per cent of all newly hired Government employees should be from ethnic minority groups, who themselves only make up 6 per cent of the Welsh population. It has another scheme that pays £5,000 to ethnic minority students who want to become teachers, money that isn't available to students if they are white. These measures, which are themselves explicitly racist, fall under the scheme ironically named the 'Anti-racist Wales Action Plan'. Put plainly, it is anti-white discrimination, and the Welsh people will not sit idly by as we are racially discriminated against in our own country. First Minister, will it be your Government that delivers the return of race-blind meritocracy in Wales?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Brif Weinidog, mae gan Lywodraeth Cymru darged lle dylai 20 y cant o'r holl weithwyr Llywodraeth sy'n cael eu cyflogi o'r newydd fod o grwpiau lleiafrifoedd ethnig, sydd eu hunain yn 6 y cant yn unig o boblogaeth Cymru. Mae ganddo gynllun arall sy'n talu £5,000 i fyfyrwyr o leiafrifoedd ethnig sydd eisiau bod yn athrawon, arian nad yw ar gael i fyfyrwyr os ydyn nhw'n wyn. Mae'r mesurau hyn, sydd eu hunain yn amlwg yn hiliol, yn dod o dan y cynllun a elwir yn eironig yn 'Gynllun Gweithredu Gwrth-hiliaeth Cymru'. Yn syml, mae'n wahaniaethu gwrth-wyn, ac ni wnaiff pobl Cymru sefyll yn ddidaro wrth i ni ddioddef gwahaniaethu hiliol yn ein gwlad ein hunain. Brif Weinidog, ai'ch Llywodraeth chi fydd yn cyflawni dychweliad meritocratiaeth hil-ddall yng Nghymru?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: I'm sure the Member is pushing the limits of what the Llywydd would deem acceptable in the Chamber. My Government believes in providing opportunities to people in a way that promotes equality of opportunity. The Member chooses to focus on the colour of skin. I would—[Interruption.] I would choose to focus on the fact that there are many people who don't have opportunities because they live in poverty, because they happen to come from a background that has not made those opportunities open to them, as they are to somebody as privileged as I have been. That is something that I would expect to be a core value of everybody in this Senedd who believes in supporting and representing all of the people of Wales, regardless of their background, regardless of the colour of their skin. It is about taking a suite of measures that we can honestly believe reflect those values that were, in many ways, the basis of the election that allowed us to have a Government of which hope was seen as a real mantra.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Rwy'n siŵr bod yr Aelod yn gwthio terfynau'r hyn y byddai'r Llywydd yn ei ystyried yn dderbyniol yn y Siambr. Mae fy Llywodraeth yn credu mewn cynnig cyfleoedd i bobl mewn ffordd sy'n hybu cyfle cyfartal. Mae'r Aelod yn dewis canolbwyntio ar liw croen. Byddwn i—[Torri ar draws.] Byddwn yn dewis canolbwyntio ar y ffaith bod llawer o bobl nad ydyn nhw'n cael cyfleoedd gan eu bod nhw'n byw mewn tlodi, oherwydd eu bod nhw'n digwydd dod o gefndir nad yw wedi gwneud y cyfleoedd hynny yn agored iddyn nhw, fel y maen nhw i rywun mor freintiedig ag yr wyf i wedi bod. Mae hynny'n rhywbeth y byddwn i'n disgwyl iddo fod yn werth craidd i bawb yn y Senedd hon sy'n credu mewn cynorthwyo a chynrychioli holl bobl Cymru, waeth beth fo'u cefndir, waeth beth yw lliw eu croen. Mae'n fater o gymryd cyfres o fesurau y gallwn ni gredu yn onest eu bod nhw'n adlewyrchu'r gwerthoedd hynny a oedd, mewn sawl ffordd, yn sail i'r etholiad a ganiataodd i ni gael Llywodraeth yr ystyriwyd gobaith yn wir fantra iddi.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: First Minister, from your previous answer I can tell that you agree with me that, when we talk about equality in Cymru, it's more than a buzz word. We’re talking about people's lives, where families working multiple jobs are struggling to get by, mums have been pushed out of work because their childcare is unaffordable, disabled people face barriers to services, racialised communities experience persistent discrimination. These pressures don’t exist in isolation; they’re the conditions in which inequality deepens and division takes hold. The consequence of this widening inequality is that, when people feel ignored or left behind, it’s fertile ground for far-right extremism—movements that thrive on misinformation, scapegoating and fear, and they target the communities already facing inequality, undermining the joint effort that we need to build a fairer Wales. So, I’d like to ask how the Government is ensuring that it’s addressing the root causes of inequality and protecting those most targeted by hate and division across Wales.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Brif Weinidog, o'ch ateb blaenorol gallaf ddweud eich bod chi'n cytuno â mi, pan fyddwn ni'n siarad am gydraddoldeb yng Nghymru, ei fod yn fwy na gair ffasiynol. Rydym ni'n sôn am fywydau pobl, lle mae teuluoedd sy'n gweithio sawl swydd yn cael trafferth yn byw, mae mamau wedi cael eu gwthio allan o waith gan nad yw eu gofal plant yn fforddiadwy, mae pobl anabl yn wynebu rhwystrau i wasanaethau, mae cymunedau sydd wedi'u hiliol yn dioddef gwahaniaethu parhaus. Nid yw'r pwysau hyn yn bodoli ar eu pen eu hunain; dyma'r amodau lle mae anghydraddoldeb yn dwysau ac y mae ymraniad yn cymryd gafael ynddyn nhw. Canlyniad yr anghydraddoldeb hwn sy'n ehangu yw pan fydd pobl yn teimlo eu bod wedi'u hanwybyddu neu eu gadael ar ôl, mae'n dir ffrwythlon ar gyfer eithafiaeth dde eithafol—mudiadau sy'n ffynnu ar gamwybodaeth, ofn a gwneud pobl yn gocyn hitio, ac maen nhw'n targedu'r cymunedau sydd eisoes yn wynebu anghydraddoldeb, gan danseilio'r ymdrech ar y cyd sydd ei angen arnom ni i adeiladu Cymru decach. Felly, hoffwn ofyn sut mae'r Llywodraeth yn sicrhau ei bod hi'n mynd i'r afael ag achosion sylfaenol anghydraddoldeb ac yn amddiffyn y rhai sy'n cael eu targedu fwyaf gan gasineb ac ymraniad ledled Cymru.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: I want to associate myself with all of the words spoken by the Member there. This isn't—. There are elements of policy here, but this is about values. This is about ensuring that, in everything we do as a Government, be it in education, in healthcare, in job creation—all of those elements where people interact with public services—or in supporting communities and putting in place policies that support cohesion, always we are driven by those values. It is something that I know unites the majority within this Senedd: the need to speak the language of tolerance. And to have a Government here that acts in a way that always promotes that cohesion and tolerance is something that is very, very important to us.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Hoffwn gysylltu fy hun â'r holl eiriau a lefarwyd gan yr Aelod yn y fan yna. Nid yw hyn yn—. Mae yna elfennau o bolisi yma, ond mae hyn yn ymwneud â gwerthoedd. Mae hyn yn ymwneud â sicrhau, ym mhopeth yr ydym ni'n ei wneud fel Llywodraeth, boed hynny ym meysydd addysg, gofal iechyd, creu swyddi—yr holl elfennau hynny lle mae pobl yn rhyngweithio â gwasanaethau cyhoeddus—neu wrth gefnogi cymunedau a rhoi polisïau ar waith sy'n cefnogi cydlyniant, ein bod ni'n cael ein hysgogi bob amser gan y gwerthoedd hynny. Mae'n rhywbeth y gwn sy'n uno'r mwyafrif o fewn y Senedd hon: yr angen i siarad iaith goddefgarwch. Ac mae bod â Llywodraeth yma sy'n gweithredu mewn ffordd sydd bob amser yn hyrwyddo'r cydlyniant a'r goddefgarwch hynny yn rhywbeth sy'n bwysig iawn, iawn i ni.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: 5. Will the First Minister provide an update on the Government's work to develop a sustainable additional learning needs service? OQ64392

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Mae cefnogi plant a phobl ifanc ag anghenion dysgu ychwanegol a sicrhau system gynaliadwy yn flaenoriaeth i’r Llywodraeth hon. Mae hyn yn hollbwysig er mwyn codi safonau a sicrhau bod y dysgwyr yma'n cael y cymorth maen nhw ei angen i ffynnu. Mi ydym ni wedi ymrwymo i weithio efo'n partneriaid i ddatblygu atebion cynaliadwy fydd yn para yn y tymor hir.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Supporting children and young people with additional learning needs and delivering a sustainable system is a priority for this Government. This is critical to raising standards and ensuring that these learners are supported to thrive. We are committed to working with our partners to develop sustainable solutions over the long term.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch, Brif Weinidog. Mae'r cyllid atodol yn gyfle mawr i wneud gwahaniaethau a dechrau gweithredu ar flaenoriaethau pobl Cymru. Mae'r cyllid yn ffocysu ar weithgareddau sy'n medru cael eu gweithredu yn y flwyddyn gyllidol hon, gan gynnwys cyllid uniongyrchol i ysgolion i sefydlogi a chefnogi'r ddarpariaeth bresennol ac sy'n galluogi dull cynaliadwy tymor hir i ddod i'r amlwg. Rwy'n ofni y bydd atal y cyllid atodol hwn yn peryglu hynny, yn cadw'r sectorau mewn sefyllfa hynod o anodd ac yn mynd yn erbyn y blaenoriaethau fe bleidleisiodd pobl Cymru drostyn nhw eleni. Er hyn, mae'n amlwg bod angen cymorth ADY arnom yma yng Nghymru. Felly, sut fydd y Llywodraeth hon yn mynd ati mewn ffordd ystyrlon ac effeithiol i gefnogi'r sector?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Thank you, First Minister. The additional funding is a great opportunity to make a difference and to start to implement the priorities of the people of Wales. The funding is focused on activities that can be implemented in this financial year, including direct funding for schools to stabilise and support the current provision and to enable a sustainable long-term approach. I fear that stopping this additional funding will put that at risk, will keep the sectors in a very difficult position and will go against the priorities that the people of Wales voted for this year. Despite this, it's clear that ALN support is needed in Wales. So, how will this Government work in a meaningful and effective way to support the sector?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Cynaliadwyedd ydy'r peth pwysig yn fan hyn, onid yw e? Dros yr wythnosau diwethaf, mae yna lot o gyfeirio wedi bod at sut rydym ni'n cyrraedd at bwynt lle mae yna gynaliadwyedd. Nid ateb tymor byr ydy hwn; mae angen dull partneriaeth go iawn, onid oes, i geisio cryfhau'r ddarpariaeth gynhwysol sydd gennym ni dros amser, a meithrin system fwy gwydn a chynaliadwy i Gymru er mwyn mynd i'r afael â'r pwysau a chwrdd â'r angen cynyddol ymysg dysgwyr.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Sustainability is the important thing here, isn't it? Over recent weeks, there have been many references to how we reach a point where there is sustainability. This is not a short-term solution; we need a real partnership approach, don't we, to try to strengthen the inclusive provision that we have over time, and to develop a more robust and sustainable system for Wales in order to tackle the pressures and to meet the increasing needs among learners.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Because we know that the pressure is great. And it's in the spirit of understanding that pressure that engagement has happened in recent weeks. And, as I laid out in a letter to the leader of the Labour group yesterday, I appreciated the determination shown by him to make sure that this was an issue on which there was focus, and it enabled us to pursue our determination to build a sustainable future for ALN provision in Wales. That is why we were able to move at pace, working with the education and Welsh language Minister in particular, to not only identify the funding against an extremely difficult funding background, but, crucially, to find a way that we can start spending this money immediately. Now, that has come about as the product of positive negotiation. What we want to do, and I think what the majority of people will sense is the right thing to do now, is to get that across the line in that spirit, which allows us, at the same time, to press ahead with spending on the NHS, on childcare and on free school meals as well, which, of course, the Labour Party agree with and I'm thankful to them for expressing that they do agree with it.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Oherwydd rydym ni'n gwybod bod y pwysau'n fawr. Ac yn ysbryd deall y pwysau hwnnw y mae ymgysylltu wedi digwydd yn ystod yr wythnosau diwethaf. Ac, fel y nodais i mewn llythyr at arweinydd y grŵp Llafur ddoe, roeddwn i'n gwerthfawrogi'r penderfyniad a ddangoswyd ganddo i wneud yn siŵr bod hwn yn fater yr oedd pwyslais arno, ac fe wnaeth ganiatáu i ni fynd ar drywydd ein penderfyniad i greu dyfodol cynaliadwy ar gyfer darpariaeth ADY yng Nghymru. Dyna pam y gallwn ni symud yn gyflym, gan weithio gyda'r Gweinidog addysg a'r Gymraeg yn arbennig, nid yn unig i nodi'r cyllid yn erbyn cefndir ariannu anodd iawn, ond, yn hollbwysig, i ddod o hyd i ffordd y gallwn ni ddechrau gwario'r arian hwn ar unwaith. Rŵan, mae hynny wedi dod fel cynnyrch o drafodaethau cadarnhaol. Yr hyn yr ydym ni eisiau ei wneud, ac rwy'n credu mai'r hyn y bydd y mwyafrif o bobl yn ei synhwyro yw'r peth iawn i'w wneud rŵan, yw cwblhau hynny yn yr ysbryd hwnnw, sy'n caniatáu i ni, ar yr un pryd, fwrw ymlaen â gwariant ar y GIG, ar ofal plant ac ar brydau ysgol am ddim hefyd, y mae'r Blaid Lafur, wrth gwrs, yn cytuno ag ef ac rwy'n ddiolchgar iddyn nhw am fynegi eu bod nhw'n cytuno ag ef.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
I'd like to start by declaring an interest. My wife and my mother both work in an education setting, which includes supporting children with ALN.

As I'm sure the First Minister is aware, conditions like autism exist on a spectrum. Different children require different levels of support and intervention. Some, with the right support, can continue in mainstream education; some can't. And then there are the countless individuals who fall somewhere in between. However, those who work within the system, those who I speak to, often tell me of a system that fails to reflect the reality, with many children in need of placement at specialist schools but stuck in a system that is often too slow to respond or sat on waiting lists for months or even years, whilst others are placed in mainstream education without the correct support packages in place, failing both the students and the schools.

First Minister, we need wholesale change and better co-ordination between health boards, mental health services and education authorities to speed up intervention. How are you going to get on and do that?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Hoffwn ddechrau trwy ddatgan buddiant. Mae fy ngwraig a fy mam ill dwy yn gweithio mewn lleoliad addysg, sy'n cynnwys cynorthwyo plant ag ADY.

Fel yr wyf i'n siŵr y mae'r Prif Weinidog yn ymwybodol, mae cyflyrau fel awtistiaeth yn bodoli ar sbectrwm. Mae gwahanol blant angen gwahanol lefelau o gymorth ac ymyrraeth. Gall rhai, gyda'r cymorth cywir, barhau mewn addysg brif ffrwd; ni all eraill. Ac yna ceir yr unigolion dirifedi sy'n syrthio rhywle rhwng y ddau. Fodd bynnag, mae'r rhai sy'n gweithio o fewn y system, y rhai yr wyf i'n siarad â nhw, yn aml yn dweud wrthyf i am system sy'n methu ag adlewyrchu'r realiti, â llawer o blant angen lle mewn ysgolion arbenigol ond yn sownd mewn system sy'n aml yn rhy araf i ymateb neu'n eistedd ar restrau aros am fisoedd neu flynyddoedd hyd yn oed, tra bod eraill yn cael eu rhoi mewn addysg brif ffrwd heb y pecynnau cymorth cywir ar waith, gan fethu'r myfyrwyr a'r ysgolion.

Brif Weinidog, mae angen newid mawr a gwell cydgysylltiad rhwng byrddau iechyd, gwasanaethau iechyd meddwl ac awdurdodau addysg i gyflymu ymyrraeth. Sut ydych chi'n mynd i fwrw ymlaen a gwneud hynny?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: The Member is quite right to point out those challenging areas. It's not just a matter of thinking of them in isolation, it's the way that they touch on each other. It is about taking that cross-Government approach. It is the way that my Ministers are approaching it. It touches on the ALN issue, again, and the need to get going on how to impact, in the most positive way, on the way policies are delivered within schools. The manifesto on which I stood made this one of the areas that we were absolutely clear we needed to gain ground on. We are confident that, in working in that cross-Government way, we can do that.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Mae'r Aelod yn gwbl gywir i dynnu sylw at y meysydd heriol hynny. Nid mater o feddwl amdanyn nhw ar wahân yn unig ydyw, mae'n fater o'r ffordd y maen nhw'n cyffwrdd â'i gilydd. Mae'n fater o fabwysiadu'r dull traws-lywodraethol hwnnw. Dyna'r ffordd y mae fy Ngweinidogion yn mynd i'r afael ag ef. Mae'n cyffwrdd ar y mater ADY, eto, a'r angen i fwrw ymlaen â sut i effeithio, yn y ffordd fwyaf cadarnhaol, ar y ffordd y mae polisïau yn cael eu darparu mewn ysgolion. Roedd y maniffesto y gwnes i sefyll ar ei sail yn gwneud hwn yn un o'r meysydd yr oeddem ni'n gwbl eglur bod angen i ni ennill tir arnyn nhw. Rydym ni'n hyderus, o weithio yn y ffordd draws-lywodraethol honno, y gallwn ni wneud hynny.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: We're committed to strengthening palliative and end-of-life care and to developing a sustainable hospice funding model. As a new Government, we're building on important foundations already established across Wales, including the quality statement, national service specification, competency framework and hospice commissioning approach. We're also working with NHS Wales, hospices and carers to improve access, strengthen the workforce, support advanced care planning and ensure long-term sustainability within the sector.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Rydym ni wedi ymrwymo i gryfhau gofal lliniarol a diwedd oes yn ogystal â datblygu model cynaliadwy i gyllido hosbisau. A ninnau'n Llywodraeth newydd, rydym ni'n adeiladu ar sylfeini pwysig a gafodd eu sefydlu ledled Cymru eisoes, gan gynnwys y datganiad ansawdd, y fanyleb gwasanaeth cenedlaethol, y fframwaith cymhwysedd a'r dull o gomisiynu hosbisau. Rydym ni'n gweithio hefyd gyda GIG Cymru, hosbisau a gofalwyr i wella mynediad, i gryfhau'r gweithlu, i gefnogi cynllunio gofal uwch a sicrhau cynaliadwyedd y sector yn yr hirdymor.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Thank you. First Minister, Cwm Taf Morgannwg University Health Board recently ran a major public engagement process regarding the future of specialist palliative care and end-of-life services across the region. One of the proposals was to close ward 6 at Ysbyty Cwm Cynon, to relocate them to Royal Glamorgan Hospital in Llantrisant. This has drawn significant local opposition and concern. Residents and local councils argue that closing the specialist beds in the Cynon valley could force terminally ill patients in Merthyr and Cynon to travel for further care.

I'm sure that the First Minister agrees with me that hospice and end-of-life services are some of the cornerstones of the Welsh healthcare system. Each year, they provide essential care and support for more than 20,000 children and adults living with terminal illness, easing pressures on the NHS by delivering vital, compassionate care within communities across Wales. However, rising demand and increasing costs are placing these services—[Interruption.] One more thing—under strain. Will the First Minister commit to providing sustainable long-term funding for hospices and end-of-life services in Wales to ensure that they can continue to deliver essential palliative and end-of-life care?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch i chi. Brif Weinidog, fe gynhaliodd Bwrdd Iechyd Prifysgol Cwm Taf Morgannwg broses eang i ymgysylltu â'r cyhoedd yn ddiweddar ynghylch dyfodol gofal lliniarol arbenigol a gwasanaethau diwedd oes ledled y rhanbarth. Un o'r cynigion oedd cau ward 6 yn Ysbyty Cwm Cynon, i'w hadleoli i Ysbyty Brenhinol Morgannwg yn Llantrisant. Mae hynny wedi ennyn gwrthwynebiad a phryder sylweddol yn lleol. Mae trigolion a chynghorau lleol yn dadlau y gallai cau'r gwelyau arbenigol yng Nghwm Cynon orfodi cleifion terfynol sâl ym Merthyr a Chynon i deithio ar gyfer gofal pellach.

Rwy'n siŵr fod y Prif Weinidog yn cytuno â mi mai gwasanaethau hosbis a diwedd oes yw rhai o gonglfeini system gofal iechyd Cymru. Bob blwyddyn, maen nhw'n darparu gofal a chefnogaeth hanfodol i fwy na 20,000 o blant ac oedolion sy'n byw gyda salwch terfynol, gan ysgafnu'r pwysau ar y GIG drwy ddarparu gofal hanfodol, caredig mewn cymunedau ledled Cymru. Serch hynny, mae'r galw a chostau cynyddol yn rhoi'r gwasanaethau hyn—[Torri ar draws.] Un peth arall—dan straen. A wnaiff y Prif Weinidog ymrwymo i ddarparu cyllid hirdymor cynaliadwy ar gyfer hosbisau a gwasanaethau diwedd oes yng Nghymru i sicrhau eu bod nhw'n gallu parhau i ddarparu gofal lliniarol hanfodol a gofal diwedd oes?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: I certainly agree with the Member on the importance of the sector. I say that as a former active member of the cross-party group in the last Senedd, and the previous one, on end-of-life care. On the particular issue of Ysbyty Cwm Cynon, I believe the health board's position is that consolidating specialist in-patient palliative care is necessary in their view to address workforce shortages and to maintain safe and sustainable specialist services. It's true to say, of course, that it is up to health boards in Wales to make those decisions. They hold the statutory responsibilities for the planning and delivery of healthcare services. They have to deliver them in a way that is tailored to the needs of their populations. But we are continuing discussions within the sector. The Cabinet Minister for Health and Care hopes to be meeting very soon, I think, with Hospices Cymru to discuss current pressures and the long-term sustainability of hospice services in Wales.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Rwy'n sicr yn cytuno â'r Aelod o ran pwysigrwydd y sector. Rwy'n dweud hynny a minnau'n gyn-aelod gweithredol o'r grŵp trawsbleidiol yn y Senedd ddiwethaf, a'r un blaenorol, ar ofal diwedd oes. O ran mater penodol Ysbyty Cwm Cynon, rwy'n credu mai safbwynt y bwrdd iechyd yw bod angen cydgrynhoi gofal lliniarol cleifion mewnol arbenigol yn eu barn nhw ar gyfer mynd i'r afael â phrinder y gweithlu a chynnal gwasanaethau arbenigol sy'n ddiogel a chynaliadwy. Mae hi'n wir dweud, wrth gwrs, mai'r byrddau iechyd yng Nghymru sy'n gwneud y penderfyniadau hyn. Y nhw sydd â'r cyfrifoldebau statudol ar gyfer cynllunio a darparu gwasanaethau gofal iechyd. Mae'n rhaid iddyn nhw gyflawni'r rhain mewn ffordd a addaswyd yn arbennig i anghenion eu poblogaethau nhw. Ond rydym ni'n dal ati i drafod yn y sector. Mae'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal yn gobeithio cyfarfod yn fuan iawn, rwy'n credu, gyda Hosbisau Cymru i drafod y pwysau ar hyn o bryd a chynaliadwyedd hirdymor gwasanaethau hosbis yng Nghymru.

Mi fydd cryfhau’r dull hwnnw, ynghyd â symud y system yn raddol tuag at atal, yn hanfodol i sicrhau cynaliadwyedd yn y tymor hir.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Dwi'n croesawu nifer o'r camau pendant a gymerwyd gan Lywodraeth Plaid Cymru ers dod i rym er mwyn mynd i'r afael â'r heriau dwys sy'n wynebu'r gwasanaeth iechyd ym Mangor Conwy Môn. Rydym ni wedi gweld ymrwymiad uniongyrchol ym Mwrdd Iechyd Prifysgol Betsi Cadwaladr ac arian ychwanegol i'r gwasanaeth iechyd yn y gyllideb atodol. Dwi'n siŵr bydd pawb yn cydnabod y gwahaniaeth y gall yr arian hwnnw ei wneud i gleifion a staff, ac mor bwysig felly yw pasio'r gyllideb y prynhawn yma. Wrth edrych tuag at y dyfodol ac i sicrhau bod y gwaith da yn parhau, mae'n rhaid annog defnydd mwy effeithiol o arian cyhoeddus yn y gwasanaeth iechyd. Gyda hynny mewn golwg, a wnaiff y Prif Weinidog roi diweddariad ar ymrwymiad y Llywodraeth i sefydlu tîm effeithiolrwydd cyllid iechyd a phryd mae'n gobeithio gweld y cam hwnnw'n dwyn ffrwyth?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: I welcome many of the steps taken by the Plaid Cymru Government since coming into power in order to address the real challenges facing the health service in Bangor Conwy Môn. We have seen a direct commitment to Betsi Cadwaladr University Health Board as well as additional funding for the health service in the supplementary budget. I'm sure that everyone would recognise the difference that that funding could make for patients and staff, and therefore how important it is that we pass the supplementary budget this afternoon. In looking to the future and to ensure that the good work can continue, we must encourage more efficient use of public funds within the health service. With that in mind, will the First Minister provide an update on the Government's commitment to establish a health finance efficiency team and when he hopes to see that being established?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Fel systemau gofal iechyd eraill, gan gynnwys mewn rhannau eraill o'r Deyrnas Unedig, mae'r gwasanaeth iechyd yma yn wynebu heriau ariannol sylweddol. Dwi'n meddwl bod hynny'n blaen i bawb. Mae angen rhagor o waith yn sicr, a chamau gweithredu, i'w roi o ar sail gynaliadwy. Mae gweithio ar yr elfen effeithlonrwydd yn bwysig iawn, iawn. Mae'r gyllideb atodol, wrth gwrs, sydd o'n blaenau ni heddiw yn cynnwys £100 miliwn o gyllid ychwanegol i gefnogi lleihau amseroedd aros, £45 miliwn o gyllid cyfalaf ar gyfer y gwasanaeth iechyd, a bydd Bwrdd Iechyd Prifysgol Betsi Cadwaladr yn elwa yn uniongyrchol o'r ffrwd ariannu honno.

Mae Ysgrifennydd y Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal, ynghyd â swyddogion, yn adolygu'r trefniadau presennol o ran effeithlonrwydd, efo'r bwriad o'u cryfhau nhw a nodi cyfres glir o gamau gweithredu erbyn diwedd y 100 diwrnod cyntaf, sydd ymhen rhyw 43 diwrnod erbyn hyn. Ond y tu hwnt, dwi'n meddwl, i'r syniad o effeithlonrwydd yn gyffredinol, mae angen dull gweithredu hirdymor yn cynnwys troi mwy a mwy at yr ataliol, ac mae'n hagwedd ni at hyn hefyd yn rhan o'n hymrwymiad 100 diwrnod cyntaf.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
As with other healthcare systems, including in other parts of the UK, the health service here faces significant financial challenges. I think that is clear to everyone. We need more work certainly, and actions, to put it on a sustainable footing. Working on the efficiency element is very, very important. The supplementary budget, of course, which we have before us today, includes £100 million of additional funding to support a reduction in waiting times, £45 million of capital funding for the health service, and the Betsi Cadwaladr University Health Board will benefit directly from that funding stream.

The Cabinet Secretary for Health and Care, as well as officials, are reviewing the current arrangements in terms of efficiency, with the intention of strengthening them and noting a clear set of actions by the end of the first 100 days, which will be in about 43 days now. But beyond the idea of efficiency in general, I think we need a long-term approach that includes turning increasingly towards the preventative agenda, and our attitude to that is also part of our first 100 days commitment.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Small and Medium-sized Businesses

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: 8. Beth mae Llywodraeth Cymru yn ei wneud i gefnogi busnesau bach a chanolig yn Sir Gaerfyrddin? OQ64424
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: 8. What is the Welsh Government doing to support small and medium-sized businesses in Carmarthenshire? OQ64424

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Small and medium-sized businesses are at the heart of Carmarthenshire's economy. We're supporting them through Business Wales, the Development Bank of Wales, SMART Innovation support, town-centre regeneration programmes, supply-chain opportunities linked to major investments such as Pentre Awel, and targeted funding that helps businesses innovate, expand and create jobs across the county.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Mae busnesau bach a chanolig wrth galon economi Sir Gaerfyrddin. Rydym ni'n eu cefnogi nhw drwy gyfrwng Busnes Cymru, Banc Datblygu Cymru, cymorth Arloesi SMART, rhaglenni adfywio canol trefi, cyfleoedd yn y gadwyn gyflenwi sy'n gysylltiedig â buddsoddiadau mawr fel Pentre Awel, a chyllid wedi'i dargedu sy'n rhoi cymorth i fusnesau ar gyfer arloesi, ehangu a chreu swyddi ledled y sir.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Diolch, First Minister. I recently spoke to owners of haulage businesses in my constituency, who tell me that it costs around £3,000 to get a driver their HGV licence for a job that can actually pay up to £50,000 a year, yet they still cannot recruit and retain drivers. They have a practical proposal: a Welsh Government loan to cover that licence cost, repaid by the driver once they're earning. In effect, an income-contingent loan that would cost the taxpayer next to nothing in the long run. England currently offers free HGV skills boot camps, but Wales does not.

And here's a wider point as well: after net migration hit a record 944,000 in 2023, justified as filling labour shortages, these Carmarthenshire businesses still can't find enough drivers. Now, I'm sure I'm going to hear the word 'Brexit' being fired from a cannon over there any second, but having spoken to these people, they tell me that it's not Brexit, it's the prohibitive cost of the licence that drivers and hauliers state is the real obstacle here. So, would you commit today to examining at least an income-contingent loan scheme for HGV licences and support these businesses to drive Wales's economy forward?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch, Brif Weinidog. Yn ddiweddar, fe fues i'n siarad â pherchnogion busnesau cludiant yn fy etholaeth i, ac maen nhw'n dweud wrthyf i ei bod hi'n costio tua £3,000 i gael trwydded cerbydau nwyddau trwm i yrrwr ar gyfer swydd sy'n gallu talu hyd at £50,000 y flwyddyn mewn gwirionedd ond nid ydyn nhw'n gallu recriwtio na chadw gyrwyr er hynny. Mae ganddyn nhw gynnig ymarferol: benthyciad gan Lywodraeth Cymru i dalu cost y drwydded honno, a gaiff ei ad-dalu gan y gyrrwr pan fydd yn ennill arian. Mewn gwirionedd, benthyciad yn ddibynnol ar incwm na fyddai'n costio dim bron â bod i'r trethdalwr yn yr hirdymor. Ar hyn o bryd maen nhw'n cynnig gwersylloedd sylfaen sgiliau cerbydau nwyddau trwm am ddim yn Lloegr, ond nid felly yng Nghymru.

A dyma bwynt ehangach hefyd: ar ôl i fudo net gyrraedd y swm uchaf erioed o 944,000 yn 2023, a gafodd ei gyfiawnhau fel datrysiad i brinder llafur, nid yw'r busnesau hyn yn Sir Gaerfyrddin yn gallu dod o hyd i ddigon o yrwyr o hyd. Nawr, rwy'n siŵr y byddaf i'n clywed y gair 'Brexit' yn cael ei danio o ganon draw fan acw ar unrhyw eiliad, ond ar ôl siarad â'r bobl hyn, maen nhw'n dweud wrthyf i nad Brexit ydyw'r achos, cost waharddol y drwydded sy'n cael ei nodi fel y rhwystr gwirioneddol i'r gyrwyr a'r cludwyr. Felly, a wnewch chi ymrwymo heddiw i archwilio o leiaf gynllun benthyciadau sy'n ddibynnol ar incwm ar gyfer trwyddedau cerbydau nwyddau trwm a chefnogi'r busnesau hyn i sbarduno economi Cymru yn ei blaen?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Well, I'll commit to considering most things, because we're always on the lookout for good ideas. I know that the barriers to the HGV sector, with drivers, come from multiple sources. Difficulty in getting test capacity, for example, is one issue that is non-devolved, of course, but we as a Government will always seek to work with UK Government to make sure that we have the capacity for testing. There are elements, I know, in my neck of the woods where the further education sector has got involved in providing pathways, perhaps, to people into the driving sector.

I'm very happy to consider what could be done, and I know I speak on behalf of the enterprise Minister in looking at how we look at the various options on the table, to recognise that this really important sector has that need—quite a crucial need, really, for an HGV sector to have enough drivers—and that that need is fulfilled.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Wel, fe wnaf i ymrwymo i ystyried y rhan fwyaf o bethau, oherwydd rydym ni'n chwilio am syniadau da bob amser. Rwy'n gwybod bod y rhwystrau i'r sector cerbydau nwyddau trwm, o ran gyrwyr, yn tarddu o sawl ffynhonnell. Mae'r anhawster gyda chapasiti'r profion, er enghraifft, yn un mater na chafodd ei ddatganoli, wrth gwrs, ond fe fyddwn ni bob amser yn y Llywodraeth hon yn ceisio gweithio gyda Llywodraeth y DU i sicrhau bod y gallu gennym ni i gynnal profion. Mae yna elfennau, rwy'n gwybod, yn fy ardal fy hun lle mae'r sector addysg bellach wedi bod â rhan wrth ddarparu llwybrau, efallai, i bobl fynd i'r sector gyrru.

Rwy'n hapus iawn i ystyried beth y gellid ei wneud, ac fe wn i fy mod i'n siarad ar ran y Gweinidog dros fenter wrth edrych ar sut y byddwn ni'n ystyried y gwahanol ddewisiadau sydd ar gael, ar gyfer cydnabod yr angen hwnnw sydd ar y sector gwirioneddol bwysig hwn—angen hanfodol iawn, mewn gwirionedd, i sector cerbydau nwyddau trwm fod â digon o yrwyr—a bod yr angen hwnnw'n cael ei ddiwallu.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Y Cynllun Gofal Plant
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: The Childcare Scheme

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: 9. Pa gamau y mae Llywodraeth Cymru yn eu cymryd i ehangu’r cynllun gofal plant ar gyfer plant dwy oed ac i gyflwyno'r cynllun yn llawn ledled Cymru? OQ64411
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: 9. What steps is the Welsh Government taking to expand the childcare scheme for two-year-olds and to fully introduce the scheme throughout Wales? OQ64411

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Wel, fel y dywedais i'n gynharach, mae’r Llywodraeth yn cyflymu’r broses o gyflwyno 12.5 awr o ofal plant wedi’i ariannu i bob plentyn dwy oed ledled Cymru. Mi ddylai’r cyllid ychwanegol yn y gyllideb atodol alluogi awdurdodau lleol i wneud cynnydd wrth gyflwyno cam cyntaf yr ehangu hwn. Dwi’n falch bod swyddogion yn cael adborth cadarnhaol gan awdurdodau lleol am y gwahaniaeth y bydd y cyllid yma’n ei wneud.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Well, as I said earlier, the Government is accelerating the roll-out of 12.5 hours of funded childcare for all two-year-olds across Wales. The additional funding in the supplementary budget should enable local authorities to make progress on this first phase of the expansion. I am pleased that officials are having positive feedback from local authorities on the difference that the funding will make.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch, Brif Weinidog, am yr ateb. Fel rhywun sydd â phrofiad uniongyrchol diweddar o'r effaith mae costau gofal plant yn ei gael ar gyllidebau teuluoedd, roeddwn mor falch o sefyll ar faniffesto oedd yn ymrwymo i gyflwyno cynllun gofal plant gwbl drawsnewidiol. Rwyf hefyd yn falch o weld y Llywodraeth yma'n bwrw ymlaen yn syth i fuddsoddi yn y sector gofal plant drwy gyllideb atodol, a chychwyn ar y gwaith o roi'r dechrau gorau i bob plentyn a chaniatáu i rieni ddychwelyd i'w gwaith. Dyna bwysigrwydd hwyluso'r gyllideb atodol i basio heddiw, er mwyn gallu bwrw ati yn syth. Felly, byddwn yn croesawu mwy o wybodaeth ar y camau nesaf y bydd y Llywodraeth yn eu cymryd i ehangu'r ddarpariaeth.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Thank you, First Minister, for that response. As one with direct recent experience of the impact that childcare costs can have on family budgets, I was so pleased to stand on a manifesto that committed to introducing a transformational childcare scheme. I'm also pleased to see the Government proceeding immediately to invest in the childcare sector through the supplementary budget, and to start the work of giving every child the best possible start and allowing parents to return to work. That's the importance of facilitating the passing of the supplementary budget, so we can proceed immediately. So, I would welcome more information on the next steps that the Government will take to expand provision.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Diolch yn fawr iawn i'r Aelod am amlygu'r pwysau gwirioneddol sydd yna, wrth gwrs, sy'n cael ei achosi gan gostau gofal plant. Er bod fy mhlant i'n mynd yn hŷn erbyn hyn, dwi'n cofio'n iawn y gost drwm oedd yna o ddarparu gofal plant, ac rydyn ni fel Llywodraeth yn benderfynol o helpu, o ran y gost ariannol, y cyfleon sy'n cael eu rhoi i blant, a'r cyfleon economaidd sy'n dod i rieni ac yn y blaen.

Mi fydd y Dirprwy Brif Weinidog yn darparu diweddariad i'r Senedd heddiw ar y broses o gyflwyno ein cynnig gofal, ynghyd â gwybodaeth am ein modelu costau. Mae'r buddsoddiad ychwanegol yma drwy'r gyllideb atodol yn mynd i'n galluogi ni i ehangu miloedd o leoedd gofal plant ychwanegol sy'n cael eu hariannu, yn canolbwyntio'n syth ar ehangu gofal plant ar gyfer plant dwy oed. Mae hwn wastad yn rhywbeth sydd yn digwydd mewn phases: y 12.5 awr, yr 20 awr, ac wedyn ymlaen at y plant ieuengaf. Dyna sut mae hwn yn cael ei gynllunio, yn cynyddu'r amlen ariannol a'r gweithlu ar yr un pryd. Ond rydyn ni'n glir bod y newid trawsnewidiol hwn yn gofyn am sector gofal plant cryf a chynaliadwy, gweithlu medrus, a model cyllido sy'n gweithio i ddarparwyr yn ogystal ag i rieni.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
I thank the Member for drawing attention to the genuine pressure that exists, which is caused by childcare costs. Even though my children are getting older now, I remember clearly the heavy costs involved in providing childcare, and we as a Government are determined to help, with regard to the financial costs, the opportunities given to children, and the economic opportunities that follow for parents and so forth.

The Deputy First Minister will provide an update to the Senedd today on the process of rolling out the childcare offer, as well as information on the cost modelling. The additional investment through the supplementary budget is going to allow us to expand thousands of additional funded childcare places, focusing immediately on expanding childcare for two-year-olds. This is always something that happens in phases: the 12.5 hours, the 20 hours, and then onwards to the youngest children. That's how it's planned, to increase the financial envelope and the workforce at the same time. But we're clear that this transformational change requires a childcare sector that is strong and sustainable, a skilled workforce, and a budget that works for providers as well as parents.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Pobl Ifanc
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Young People

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: 10. Beth mae Llywodraeth Cymru yn ei wneud i gefnogi pobl ifanc nad ydynt mewn addysg, cyflogaeth na hyfforddiant? OQ64426
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: 10. What is the Welsh Government doing to support young people who are not in education, employment or training? OQ64426

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Supporting young people who are not in education, employment or training is a priority for this Government. We're investing in support that helps young people develop skills, build confidence and move into education, training, employment or self-employment. Alongside this, our 'Wales means business' agenda is focused on growing Welsh businesses, attracting investment and creating more high-quality jobs across Wales.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Mae cefnogi pobl ifanc nad ydyn nhw mewn addysg, cyflogaeth na hyfforddiant yn flaenoriaeth i'r Llywodraeth hon. Rydym ni'n buddsoddi mewn cymorth sy'n cynorthwyo pobl ifanc i ddatblygu sgiliau, magu hyder a symud i addysg, hyfforddiant, cyflogaeth neu hunangyflogaeth. Ochr yn ochr â hyn, mae ein hagenda 'Mae Cymru ar agor ar gyfer busnes' yn canolbwyntio ar feithrin busnesau yng Nghymru, denu buddsoddiad a chreu mwy o swyddi o ansawdd uchel ledled Cymru.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch, Brif Weinidog. Earlier this year, Premier Forest Products in Newport became the first private sector company to sign the Welsh Government's corporate parenting charter. Working in partnership with Newport City Council, Premier Forest provides paid work placements for care-experienced young people. Opportunities are offered across all departments, helping participants gain practical experience of the workplace and transition into employment. Terry Edgell, chief executive officer of Premier Forest Products, is clear that commercial success comes with social responsibility, and I've seen and heard first-hand what a difference this makes to young people, the company and also the workforce. So, I'd like to know: what is the Welsh Government doing to encourage and support more employers to give opportunities like this to care-experienced young people across Wales?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch, Brif Weinidog. Yn gynharach eleni, Premier Forest Products yng Nghasnewydd oedd y cwmni sector preifat cyntaf i arwyddo siarter rhianta corfforaethol Llywodraeth Cymru. Gan weithio mewn partneriaeth â Chyngor Dinas Casnewydd, mae cwmni Premier Forest yn darparu lleoliadau gwaith â thâl i bobl ifanc sydd â phrofiad o ofal. Mae cyfleoedd yn cael eu cynnig ar draws pob adran, sy'n helpu cyfranogwyr i ennill profiad ymarferol o'r gweithle a throsglwyddo i gyflogaeth. Mae Terry Edgell, prif swyddog gweithredol Premier Forest Products, yn eglur o ran bod llwyddiant masnachol yn dod gyda chyfrifoldeb cymdeithasol, ac rwyf i wedi gweld a chlywed yn uniongyrchol pa wahaniaeth y mae hyn yn ei wneud i bobl ifanc, i'r cwmni a'r gweithlu hefyd. Felly, fe hoffwn i gael gwybod: beth mae Llywodraeth Cymru yn ei wneud i annog a chefnogi mwy o gyflogwyr i roi cyfleoedd fel hyn i bobl ifanc sydd â phrofiad o ofal ledled Cymru?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Thank you, and congratulations to Terry and the team at Premier Forest Products. It does take good employers to show the way as well, so my gratitude is genuine to the team there in Newport. It takes a whole host of things to come together, doesn't it? It can be Government programmes, both devolved and non-devolved. It can be Jobs Growth Wales. It can be Communities for Work. It can be the Economic Inactivity Trailblazer. It could be work being done within the further education and skills sector itself. Medr is currently developing a more flexible apprenticeship programme for 2027, aligned to employer demand. We've got to make sure that it's aligned to the needs of those young people that we need to bring into the system. Careers Wales is still important in this, and making sure that they're there, at the right place, at the right time, to point young people in the right direction. So, it's an all-Government approach, but finding those trailblazing companies is really important to show others that it is in their interests to make sure that they provide opportunities for young people who otherwise could be missed.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch i chi, a llongyfarchiadau i Terry a'r tîm yn Premier Forest Products. Mae'n rhaid i gyflogwyr da ddangos y ffordd hefyd, felly mae fy niolchgarwch i'n ddiffuant iawn i'r tîm yno yng Nghasnewydd. Mae'n rhaid cael llaweroedd o bethau at ei gilydd, onid oes? Fe all hyn olygu rhaglenni gan y Llywodraethau, datganoledig a heb eu datganoli. Fe all hyn olygu Twf Swyddi Cymru. Fe all hyn olygu Cymunedau am Waith. Fe all hyn olygu Arloeswr Anweithgarwch Economaidd. Fe allai olygu gwaith sy'n cael ei wneud yn y sector addysg bellach a sgiliau. Ar hyn o bryd mae Medr yn datblygu rhaglen brentisiaeth fwy hyblyg ar gyfer 2027, sy'n cyd-fynd â'r galw sydd gan gyflogwyr. Mae'n rhaid i ni sicrhau y bydd yn cyd-fynd ag anghenion y bobl ifanc hynny y mae angen i ni eu tynnu nhw i mewn i'r system. Mae Gyrfa Cymru yn dal i fod yn bwysig yn hyn o beth, a sicrhau eu bod nhw yno, yn y lle iawn, ar yr adeg iawn, i roi'r bobl ifanc ar ben y ffordd. Felly, mae hwnnw'n ddull gweithredu i Lywodraeth gyfan, ond mae dod o hyd i'r cwmnïau arloesol hynny yn bwysig iawn er mwyn dangos i eraill ei bod hi'n fuddiol iddyn nhw sicrhau eu bod nhw'n estyn cyfleoedd i bobl ifanc y gellid eu colli nhw fel arall.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Ac yn olaf, Brif Weinidog, cwestiwn 11 gan James Evans.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: And finally, First Minister, question 11 from James Evans.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Welsh Government uses a resource allocation formula to distribute the majority of NHS funding according to the relative health needs of the population served by each health board. The formula is commonly referred to as the local health board resource allocation formula.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Mae Llywodraeth Cymru yn defnyddio fformiwla dyrannu adnoddau i ddosbarthu'r rhan fwyaf o gyllid y GIG yn ôl anghenion iechyd cymharol y boblogaeth syn cael eu gwasanaethau gan bob bwrdd iechyd. Fe gyfeirir at y fformiwla honno'n gyffredin fel fformiwla dyrannu adnoddau'r bwrdd iechyd lleol.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Thank you for your answer, First Minister. I've raised on the floor of this Chamber a number of times the decisions that the Powys Teaching Health Board have taken: reducing bed numbers, closing hospitals, reducing access to minor injury units, ward closures, and also delaying care across the border in England to meet their financial challenges. Your legislative statement this afternoon is bringing forward a rural-proofing element to legislation. I'm interested, First Minister, in whether that rural-proofing then applies to rural health boards, to make sure that the funding that they receive actually protects the people who pay the same amount of tax as anybody else in this room, but receive a lower standard of service. So, I'd like to hear from you: what is your Government going to do to protect those rural health boards to make sure they get the funding they need, so my constituents can get the care they need and they pay for in their taxes?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch i chi am eich ateb, Brif Weinidog. Rwyf i wedi codi'r penderfyniadau a wnaeth Bwrdd Iechyd Addysgu Powys ar lawr y Siambr hon sawl gwaith: lleihau nifer y gwelyau, cau ysbytai, cyfyngu mynediad i unedau mân anafiadau, cau wardiau, ac oedi gofal ar draws y ffin yn Lloegr i gwrdd â'i heriau ariannol ei hun hefyd. Mae eich datganiad deddfwriaethol chi'r prynhawn yma yn cyflwyno elfen o brawfesur gwledig i'r ddeddfwriaeth. Fe fyddai hi'n dda iawn gen i wybod, Brif Weinidog, a yw'r prawfesur hwnnw'n berthnasol i fyrddau iechyd gwledig wedyn, i wneud yn siŵr bod y cyllid y maen nhw'n ei gael yn diogelu'r bobl sy'n talu'r un swm o dreth ag y mae unrhyw un arall sydd yn yr ystafell hon, ond sy'n cael safon is o wasanaeth. Felly, fe hoffwn i glywed gennych chi: beth fydd eich Llywodraeth chi'n ei wneud i amddiffyn y byrddau iechyd hynny mewn ardaloedd gwledig i sicrhau eu nhw'n cael y cyllid sydd ei angen arnyn nhw, er mwyn i'm hetholwyr i gael y gofal sydd ei angen arnyn nhw ac y maen nhw'n talu amdano gyda'u trethi?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Daeth y Dirprwy Lywydd (Kerry Ferguson) i’r Gadair.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: The Deputy Presiding Officer (Kerry Ferguson) took the Chair.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: The Member is right, and I expect every Member here to want to make sure that the health board serving their constituency is funded according to its need. I should say that the resource allocation formula does take into account the excess costs of rurality. It is one of the factors that is factored into that particular formula. We've got to make sure that it's effective, that it works. Does rural-proofing have a direct impact on that particular formula? I wouldn't say that the legislation that we have in mind would lead to there being a direct impact, but it's a principle. What that legislation shows is that this is a Government that, as a matter of principle, wants to make sure that no rural part of Wales is left behind because of its rurality. That should be as relevant in health as in anything else.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Mae'r Aelod yn iawn, ac rwy'n disgwyl i bob Aelod yma fod yn awyddus i sicrhau y bydd y bwrdd iechyd sy'n gwasanaethu eu hetholaethau nhw eu hunain yn cael ei ariannu yn ôl yr angen yno. Fe ddylwn i ddweud bod y fformiwla dyrannu adnoddau yn cymryd costau dros ben yng nghefn gwlad i ystyriaeth. Dyma un o'r ffactorau sy'n cael eu hystyried yn y fformiwla benodol honno. Mae'n rhaid i ni sicrhau bod hynny'n effeithiol, ac yn gweithio. A yw prawfesur gwledig yn cael effaith uniongyrchol ar y fformiwla benodol honno? Ni fyddwn i'n dweud y byddai'r ddeddfwriaeth sydd gennym ni mewn golwg yn arwain at effaith uniongyrchol, ond mae'r egwyddor yno. Yr hyn y mae'r ddeddfwriaeth honno'n ei arddangos yw bod hon yn Llywodraeth sydd, fel mater o egwyddor, yn awyddus i sicrhau nad oes ardal wledig yng Nghymru yn cael ei gadael ar ôl am ei bod hi'n ardal wledig. Fe ddylai hynny fod yr un mor berthnasol o ran iechyd ag o ran unrhyw beth arall.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Thank you, First Minister.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Effeithiolrwydd Llywodraeth a'r Cyfansoddiad
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Government Effectiveness and the Constitution
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: 1. Pa fesurau y mae Llywodraeth Cymru yn eu defnyddio i asesu effeithiolrwydd Llywodraeth ar draws adrannau? OQ64378
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: 1. What measures is the Welsh Government using to assess the effectiveness of Government across departments? OQ64378

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Effeithiolrwydd Llywodraeth a'r Cyfansoddiad
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Government Effectiveness and the Constitution
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Member_job_title_English: Cabinet Minister for Government Effectiveness and the Constitution
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Member_job_title_Welsh: Y Gweinidog Cabinet dros Effeithiolrwydd Llywodraeth a’r Cyfansoddiad
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: The Welsh Government uses a range of measures to assess effectiveness across departments, depending on the policy area and the outcomes being delivered. These include management information, official statistics, evaluation evidence, financial and performance reporting, and feedback from service users and those with lived experience.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Mae Llywodraeth Cymru yn defnyddio ystod o fesurau i asesu effeithiolrwydd ar draws adrannau, yn ddibynnol ar faes y polisi a'r canlyniadau a gaiff eu cyflawni. Mae'r rhain yn cynnwys gwybodaeth am eu rheolaeth, ystadegau swyddogol, tystiolaeth o werthuso, adroddiadau ariannol ac am berfformiad, ac adborth oddi wrth ddefnyddwyr y gwasanaethau ac oddi wrth y rhai sydd â phrofiad bywyd.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Effeithiolrwydd Llywodraeth a'r Cyfansoddiad
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Government Effectiveness and the Constitution
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Thank you, Minister. I'm glad to hear it's so full. Your published ministerial responsibilities include official statistics, including the census, social research and the national survey for Wales. Effective government depends on understanding how Wales is changing and ensuring that future planning reflects that evidence. What research has your department undertaken into the demographic changes in Wales since the implementation of the nation of sanctuary policy and how are those findings being incorporated into the evidence used to forecast future demand for housing, NHS services, school places, transport infrastructure and other public services across Wales? If those demographic changes are not being factored into Government planning, how can you be confident that your forecasts accurately reflect the future needs of Wales? This is not being divisive or any other adjectives you may wish to throw at our party; the people of Wales deserve to understand how the Government determines the future requirements of our nation, and your portfolio is central to ensuring that those decisions are informed by robust evidence and accurate data. Thank you.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch i chi, Weinidog. Rwy'n falch o glywed bod y gwaith mor llawn. Mae eich cyfrifoldebau gweinidogol cyhoeddedig chi'n cynnwys ystadegau swyddogol, gan gynnwys y cyfrifiad, ymchwil gymdeithasol ac arolwg cenedlaethol Cymru. Mae llywodraeth effeithiol yn dibynnu ar ddealltwriaeth o sut mae Cymru yn newid a sicrhau bod cynllunio i'r dyfodol yn adlewyrchu'r dystiolaeth honno. Pa ymchwil a wnaeth eich adran chi i'r newidiadau demograffig yng Nghymru ers gweithrediad polisi'r genedl noddfa a sut mae'r canfyddiadau hynny'n cael eu hymgorffori yn y dystiolaeth sy'n cael ei defnyddio i ragweld y galw am dai, gwasanaethau'r GIG, lleoedd mewn ysgolion, seilwaith trafnidiaeth a gwasanaethau cyhoeddus eraill ledled Cymru yn y dyfodol? Os nad yw'r newidiadau demograffig hynny'n cael eu hystyried yng nghynlluniau'r Llywodraeth, sut allwch chi fod â hyder fod eich rhagolygon chi'n adlewyrchu anghenion Cymru i'r dyfodol yn iawn? Nid ystyr hyn yw ceisio creu ymraniad nac unrhyw beth arall y byddech chi'n hoffi cyhuddo ein plaid ni ohono efallai; mae pobl Cymru yn haeddu cael deall sut mae'r Llywodraeth yn penderfynu ar anghenion ein cenedl ni yn y dyfodol, ac mae eich portffolio chi'n ganolog o ran sicrhau bod y penderfyniadau hynny'n cael eu llywio gan dystiolaeth gadarn a data cywir. Diolch i chi.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Effeithiolrwydd Llywodraeth a'r Cyfansoddiad
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Government Effectiveness and the Constitution
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Thank you. I can offer the Member some reassurance here, because my colleagues in the statistics team plan meticulously based on the evidence, based on the demographic figures, and based on the whole range of factors that impact on the population of Wales, on the health of Wales, on the economy of Wales. The Member will be familiar with a number of the statistical publications that appear on a weekly basis, if not more so, from the statistics team that undertake that detailed analysis. You will also be familiar with the fact that those statistics teams look at the future population of Wales and the changing demographics in local areas. So, I can offer that reassurance to the Member.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch i chi. Rwy'n gallu cynnig rhywfaint o sicrwydd i'r Aelod yn hyn o beth oherwydd mae fy nghydweithwyr i yn y tîm ystadegau yn cynllunio yn ofalus ar sail tystiolaeth, ar sail y ffigurau demograffig, ac ar sail yr ystod gyfan o ffactorau sy'n effeithio ar boblogaeth Cymru, ar iechyd Cymru, ac ar economi Cymru. Mae'r Aelod yn siŵr o fod yn gyfarwydd â nifer o'r cyhoeddiadau ystadegol sy'n ymddangos yn wythnosol, os nad yn fwy aml ha hynny, oddi wrth y tîm ystadegau sy'n ymgymryd â'r dadansoddiad manwl hwnnw. Rydych chi'n siŵr o fod yn gyfarwydd hefyd â'r ffaith fod y timau ystadegau hynny'n ystyried poblogaeth Cymru yn y dyfodol a'r ddemograffeg newidiol mewn ardaloedd lleol. Felly, fe allaf i gynnig y sicrwydd hwnnw i'r Aelod.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Effeithiolrwydd Llywodraeth a'r Cyfansoddiad
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Government Effectiveness and the Constitution
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: If the Government's effectiveness is itself constantly being reviewed and reset, does that suggest that the current measures aren't actually working? How many more reviews will be required before Ministers can demonstrate sustained improvement? In short, how many reviews are there and will there be yet another review of the outcome of that review?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Os yw effeithiolrwydd y Llywodraeth ei hun yn cael ei adolygu a'i ailosod yn gyson, a yw hynny'n awgrymu nad yw'r mesurau cyfredol yn gweithio mewn gwirionedd? Faint o adolygiadau eraill a fydd eu hangen cyn y gall Gweinidogion arddangos gwelliant parhaus? Yn gryno iawn, faint o adolygiadau sydd yna ac a fydd yna adolygiad arall eto o ganlyniad yr adolygiad hwnnw?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Effeithiolrwydd Llywodraeth a'r Cyfansoddiad
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Government Effectiveness and the Constitution
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: I do fear the Member is a little pessimistic about our plans for Government efficiency and delivery on outcomes. I set out in my oral statement, and I've set out in this Senedd before, how we're going to focus on outcomes. What I'm doing and what we're doing as a team in the Cabinet Office, supporting my colleagues right across Government, is ensuring that every one of our plans, every one of our developments, is focused on changing the lives of the people of Wales for the better. That is what we will do. That is what we will continue to do. Again, as I alluded to in a previous contribution to this Senedd, the first 100 days puts the foundation blocks in place. We will then move rapidly into that delivery phase and ensure that the lives of the people of Wales are duly improved.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Rwy'n ofni bod yr Aelod ychydig yn besimistaidd ynglŷn â'n cynlluniau ni ar gyfer effeithlonrwydd y Llywodraeth a chyflawni canlyniadau. Fe wnes i nodi yn fy natganiad llafar, ac fe wnes i nodi yn y Senedd hon o'r blaen, sut y byddwn ni'n canolbwyntio ar ganlyniadau. Yr hyn yr wyf i'n ei wneud a'r hyn yr ydym ni'n ei wneud yn ein tîm ni yn Swyddfa'r Cabinet, gan roi cefnogaeth i'm cyd-Aelodau ar draws y Llywodraeth gyfan, yw sicrhau bod pob un o'n cynlluniau ni, pob un o'n datblygiadau ni, yn canolbwyntio ar newid bywydau pobl Cymru er gwell. Dyna beth fyddwn ni'n ei wneud. Dyna beth fyddwn ni'n dal ati i'w wneud. Unwaith eto, fel roeddwn i'n cyfeirio at hynny mewn cyfraniad blaenorol i'r Senedd hon, mae'r 100 diwrnod cyntaf yn gosod y cerrig sylfaen yn eu lle. Yna fe fyddwn ni'n symud yn gyflym i'r cyfnod cyflawni hwnnw ac yn sicrhau bod bywydau pobl Cymru yn cael eu gwella fel y dylid.
