XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
I'd like to welcome the Minister to her post. I'll stop the pleasantries here because people are watching the clock and we'll be here all night. So, anyway, I'll move on to your statement, Minister.

It says here that you've had bilaterals with Cabinet Ministers and Deputy Ministers across Government. That's lovely, but I'd like to know what the next steps of those are going to be, really, because if we don't know what's coming out of it, they're just lovely meetings to have, aren't they? You said here as well that you've talked to the First Minister and that Government decision making will be informed by a shared focus on public health. Well, I think we can all agree with that, but what does that look like in practice? We've heard these things before, and it would be quite good if we could get some understanding today as to what actually that looks like.

You did say that officials and ministerial and cross-governance and arrangements are all being established. Fantastic, but what does this mean? How much is this going to cost the Welsh civil service, in terms of having all these cross-ministerial portfolios? Is this more civil servants to do this? Is this going to be managed within the current health portfolio? You also mentioned, further down in your statement, creating a new budget line within the Government's overall budget-setting process. Is there a risk with that, even though I'm not against it in principle, that we could end up with a bit of silo working here: that, actually, other departments are all chipping in, trying to look for this pot of money, while, actually, if it sat directly within the departments, it would be easier to spend? If the cross-governmental work was focused on prevention, you maybe wouldn't need a budget line there. I'm sure the Finance Committee would be quite pleased if it wasn't there, as it's something else to look at.

You also talked about weight-loss medication. This is something I've been quite involved in, actually. I haven't taken it personally. But I think one thing we have to be careful with, with weight-loss medication, is that, yes, it is changing lives, but it's not changing lifestyles. It cannot be seen as a silver bullet to losing weight long term, because we do know about the longer term health impacts, with osteoporosis in women, with people with cardiovascular problems emerging from these jabs, so I'd just like to know—. There needs to be a way for people to get off the treadmill, as such, of taking these jabs. So, I'd like to know what work you're doing with primary care to understand how you can work with local gyms, leisure facilities, so that when people are accessing weight-loss medication, their lifestyle is changing along with their life, because if you don't, it's just a vicious circle: you'll come off it, you'll put weight back on again, and you're back on the jabs and then end up in A&E with longer term problems, and that's no way to help our health service.

You did talk about working quite closely with the wider portfolio across health. I'd be interested to know how much money you're intending to move into the prevention agenda. I know the Cabinet Minister for sport is here as well, and the Government talked an awful lot during the election period about moving money into that portfolio. So, it would be quite good today to get some figures on how much of that prevention agenda is going to be delivered there and what proportion of that is the budget. I think that's really important.

You also mentioned working with the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability. I think it's very important. We talk about healthy food; I'm a big advocate of that. I know there were Members in the Conservative Party who brought forward a food Bill, which was supported across the Chamber, which is really important. But I think we need to make sure we've got good-quality food in schools. We've all seen the scandal with Thai chicken in our schools. That's not the sort of food we want to be putting into our kids. So, the prevention agenda is moving money into the schools' budget, so you can make sure that they can afford those good things in schools, and not imported food from across the world.

What else here? Lung screening. You talked about a lung screening programme. Well, we had the pilot in the previous Senedd. That was a good success story that came out of it. I'm pleased you're rolling that out further and going to develop that. The one thing that was raised at the time was chronic obstructive pulmonary disease screening. If we don't embed COPD screening as part of that lung cancer screening process, you're literally having another test for something else. So, sometimes, it's cheaper to do it all at the same time. Yes, you might be double-diagnosing somebody, but if someone's got lung cancer, you can almost, at the same time, say they've got COPD, or they're developing it, or they have COPD and do not have cancer. So, to get it done first time is the right approach, rather than having numerous different tests for people. Treat it once and get it done with.

Then you also talked about substance misuse. I know the Deputy Minister for mental health is also sat to your side. To deal with substance abuse—I think we have to look as well—you have to treat the individual, not the offence, as such. And if you are going to move to try and address this problem, mental health support has to be there. I know when Lynne Neagle, for example, was the Minister for mental health, she actually laboured on this quite a lot: that if you do not put the mental health support in place to support people on their substance misuse journey, whether that's drugs or alcohol, you're just going to have the revolving door of people getting clean and then coming back in again, because you've not dealt with the trauma that's led people there in the first place.

And in the interests of time, Deputy Presiding Officer, I think I've taken my five minutes, even though I said I was going to be quite brief. So, if you could answer some of those questions, Deputy Minister, I'd be very much obliged. Diolch.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Hoffwn groesawu'r Gweinidog i'w swydd. Fe wnaf ddiwedd y moeseiriau yn y fan yma oherwydd mae pobl yn edrych ar y cloc a byddwn ni yma drwy'r nos. Felly, beth bynnag, rwyf am symud ymlaen at eich datganiad, Weinidog.

Mae'n dweud yma eich bod chi wedi cael trafodaethau dwyochrog gyda Gweinidogion y Cabinet a Dirprwy Weinidogion ar draws y Llywodraeth. Mae hynny'n hyfryd, ond hoffwn wybod beth fydd y camau nesaf, mewn gwirionedd, oherwydd os nad ydym yn gwybod beth fydd yn deillio o hynny, dim ond cyfarfodydd hyfryd i'w cael ydyn nhw, onid e? Dywedoch chi yma hefyd eich bod wedi siarad â'r Prif Weinidog ac y bydd proses y Llywodraeth o wneud penderfyniadau yn cael ei llywio gan ffocws ar y cyd ar iechyd y cyhoedd. Wel, rwy'n credu y gallwn ni gyd gytuno â hynny, ond sut mae hynny'n edrych yn ymarferol? Rydyn ni wedi clywed y pethau hyn o'r blaen, a byddai'n eithaf braf pe baem yn gallu cael rhywfaint o ddealltwriaeth heddiw o sut mae hynny'n edrych mewn gwirionedd.

Fe wnaethoch chi ddweud bod swyddogion a threfniadau gweinidogol a thraws-lywodraethol i gyd yn cael eu sefydlu. Gwych, ond beth mae hyn yn ei olygu? Faint y bydd hyn yn ei gostio i wasanaeth sifil Cymru, o ran cael yr holl bortffolios traws-weinidogol hyn? A yw hyn yn golygu mwy o weision sifil i wneud hyn? A fydd hyn yn cael ei reoli o fewn y portffolio iechyd presennol? Fe wnaethoch chi hefyd sôn, ymhellach i lawr yn eich datganiad, am greu llinell gyllideb newydd o fewn proses gyffredinol gosod cyllideb y Llywodraeth. A oes risg gyda hynny, er nad wyf yn ei wrthwynebu mewn egwyddor, y gallem weld ychydig o weithio heb ymwneud ag eraill yma? Hynny yw, mewn gwirionedd, adrannau eraill i gyd yn ceisio chwilio am y pot hwn o arian, ond mewn gwirionedd, pe bai'n eistedd yn uniongyrchol o fewn yr adrannau, byddai'n haws ei wario. Pe bai'r gwaith traws-lywodraethol yn canolbwyntio ar atal, efallai na fyddai angen llinell gyllideb arnoch. Rwy'n siŵr y byddai'r Pwyllgor Cyllid yn eithaf hapus pe na bai yno, gan ei fod yn rhywbeth arall i edrych arno.

Fe wnaethoch chi hefyd sôn am feddyginiaeth colli pwysau. Mae hyn yn rhywbeth rydw i wedi bod yn ymwneud ag ef yn sylweddol, mewn gwirionedd. Dydw i ddim wedi ei gymryd fy hun. Ond rwy'n credu bod yna un peth y mae'n rhaid i ni fod yn ofalus yn ei gylch o ran meddyginiaeth colli pwysau, sef ei fod yn newid bywydau, ond nid yw'n newid ffordd o fyw. Ni ellir ei ystyried fel un ateb syml ar gyfer colli pwysau yn y tymor hir, oherwydd rydyn ni'n gwybod am yr effeithiau iechyd tymor hwy, gydag osteoporosis mewn menywod, gyda phobl â phroblemau cardiofasgwlaidd yn dod i'r amlwg yn sgil y pigiadau hyn, felly hoffwn wybod—. Mae angen ffordd i alluogi pobl i ddod oddi ar y felin draed, o gymryd y brechiadau hyn. Felly, hoffwn wybod pa waith yr ydych chi'n ei wneud gyda gofal sylfaenol i ddeall sut y gallwch chi weithio gyda champfeydd lleol, cyfleusterau hamdden, fel bod ffordd o fyw pobl yn newid yn ogystal â'u bywyd pan fyddant yn cael mynediad at feddyginiaeth colli pwysau, oherwydd os nad ydych chi'n gwneud hynny, dim ond cylch dieflig ydyw: byddwch chi'n dod oddi arni, byddwch chi'n rhoi pwysau yn ôl eto, ac rydych chi'n ôl ar y pigiadau ac yna'n cael eich hun yn yr adran damweiniau ac achosion brys gyda phroblemau tymor hwy, ac nid yw hynny'n ffordd i helpu ein gwasanaeth iechyd.

Fe wnaethoch chi sôn am weithio'n eithaf agos gyda'r portffolio ehangach ar draws iechyd. Byddai gen i ddiddordeb mewn gwybod faint o arian rydych chi'n bwriadu ei symud i mewn i'r agenda atal. Rwy'n gwybod bod y Gweinidog Cabinet dros chwaraeon yma hefyd, ac mae'r Llywodraeth wedi siarad yn helaeth yn ystod cyfnod yr etholiad am symud arian i'r portffolio hwnnw. Felly, byddai'n eithaf braf heddiw cael rhai ffigurau o ran faint o'r agenda atal honno sy'n mynd i gael ei chyflawni a pha gyfran o hynny yw'r gyllideb. Rwy'n credu bod hynny'n bwysig iawn.

Fe wnaethoch chi hefyd sôn am weithio gyda'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd. Rwy'n credu ei fod yn bwysig iawn. Rydyn ni'n siarad am fwyd iach; rwy'n eiriolwr mawr dros hynny. Rwy'n gwybod bod Aelodau yn y Blaid Geidwadol wedi cyflwyno Bil bwyd, a gefnogwyd ar draws y Siambr, sy'n bwysig iawn. Ond rwy'n credu bod angen i ni wneud yn siŵr bod gennym fwyd o ansawdd da mewn ysgolion. Rydyn ni i gyd yn ymwybodol o'r sgandal ynghylch cyw iâr Thai yn ein hysgolion. Nid dyna'r math o fwyd rydyn ni eisiau ei roi i'n plant. Felly, mae'r agenda atal yn symud arian i gyllideb ysgolion, fel y gallwch wneud yn siŵr eu bod yn gallu fforddio'r pethau da hynny mewn ysgolion, ac nid bwyd wedi'i fewnforio o bob cwr o'r byd.

Beth arall sydd yma? Sgrinio ysgyfaint. Fe wnaethoch chi siarad am raglen sgrinio ysgyfaint. Wel, cawsom y cynllun treialu yn y Senedd flaenorol. Roedd honno'n stori o lwyddiant. Rwy'n falch eich bod chi'n cyflwyno hynny ymhellach ac yn mynd i ddatblygu hynny. Yr un peth a godwyd ar y pryd oedd sgrinio clefyd rhwystrol cronig yr ysgyfaint. Os nad ydym yn ymgorffori sgrinio clefyd rhwystrol cronig yr ysgyfaint fel rhan o'r broses sgrinio canser yr ysgyfaint, rydych chi'n llythrennol yn cael prawf arall ar gyfer rhywbeth arall. Felly, weithiau, mae'n rhatach gwneud y cyfan ar yr un pryd. Ie, efallai eich bod chi'n cael diagnosis dwbl, ond os oes gan rywun ganser yr ysgyfaint, gallwch bron, ar yr un pryd, ddweud bod ganddyn nhw glefyd rhwystrol cronig yr ysgyfaint, neu eu bod yn ei ddatblygu, neu fod ganddyn nhw glefyd rhwystrol cronig yr ysgyfaint ond nid oes ganddyn nhw ganser. Felly, ei wneud y tro cyntaf yw'r dull cywir, yn hytrach na chael nifer o brofion gwahanol. Ei drin unwaith a dyna ni.

Yna fe wnaethoch chi hefyd siarad am gamddefnyddio sylweddau. Rwy'n gwybod bod y Dirprwy Weinidog dros iechyd meddwl hefyd yn eistedd wrth eich ochr chi. I ymdrin â chamddefnyddio sylweddau—rwy'n credu bod yn rhaid i ni edrych hefyd—mae'n rhaid i chi drin yr unigolyn, nid y drosedd. Ac os ydych chi'n mynd i geisio mynd i'r afael â'r broblem hon, mae'n rhaid i gefnogaeth iechyd meddwl fod yno. Rwy'n gwybod pan oedd Lynne Neagle, er enghraifft, yn Weinidog dros iechyd meddwl, roedd hi'n gweithio'n galed ar hyn: os nad ydych chi'n rhoi'r cymorth iechyd meddwl ar waith i gefnogi pobl ar eu taith camddefnyddio sylweddau, boed hynny'n gyffuriau neu'n alcohol, rydych chi'n mynd i gael y drws tro pan fo pobl yn rhoi gorau i gamddefnyddio ac yna yn dod yn ôl i mewn i'r byd hwnnw eto, oherwydd nad ydych wedi ymdrin â'r trawma sydd wedi gwneud i bobl gamddefnyddio yn y lle cyntaf.

Ac o ran amser, Ddirprwy Lywydd, rwy'n credu fy mod wedi cymryd fy mhum munud, er fy mod wedi dweud fy mod i'n mynd i fod yn eithaf cryno. Felly, pe gallech chi ateb rhai o'r cwestiynau hynny, Ddirprwy Weinidog, byddwn yn ddiolchgar iawn. Diolch.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 6. Datganiad gan y Dirprwy Weinidog dros Iechyd Cyhoeddus ac Ataliol: Blaenoriaethau ar gyfer Iechyd Cyhoeddus ac Ataliol
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 6. Statement by the Deputy Minister for Public and Preventative Health: Priorities for Public and Preventative Health
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Thanks for the contribution and for the welcome into the role. In terms of the bilaterals and the shared Government understanding, I think this is the first time we've ever had this discussion across Government level. I think there have been lots of pockets of good practice over a number of years, but nothing embedded, nothing strategic, no discussion about the impact of spend on the population of Wales in other portfolio areas.

So, the bilaterals have been really good to kick that process off in terms of just seeing where we can work together. For example, you mentioned food and a discussion with the Cabinet Minister for rural resilience. That's not just a bilateral between me and that Cabinet Minister; we're talking about education, we're talking about our planning system, we're talking about the economy and supporting our food businesses. So, that's what this approach is absolutely about, to make sure we don't miss those opportunities. And if we look at the approach to food during the last Government, it was quite narrowly focused, and this is absolutely building on the work that you mentioned by your previous colleague on the food Bill, to make sure that it is a whole-system approach.

I absolutely agree with you in terms of the quality of food in schools, but also teaching our young people about food skills and making sure that we understand where our food comes from, supporting our brilliant agricultural industry, and looking at our procurement rules. So, this is not just something for food; this is absolutely health prevention, looking at the economy. So, those bilaterals have kicked off that discussion while we work out how we make sure that these are embedded discussions early on in every policy development—that we look at preventing ill health and reducing the health inequality that we've got and making sure it's a cross-Government approach. And that's my role—to make sure that we don't miss those opportunities while we work out the mechanics, and that that is replicated on the official level as well. These conversations, potentially, have never happened before in these policy areas, so it's making sure that that's embedded so that it's systematic and strategic that we really do look at health inequality and look at preventative health measures. 

In terms of the budgets and the costs, you raise some interesting points there in terms of how that will be developed. You're right in terms of a new budget line. I think the first step that we're grappling with now is the definition of 'prevention', especially if we are committed to increased spend on prevention over this Senedd term. How do we define that is really important—how do we define current activity within health and social care, but also in the other portfolio areas as we move to shift resources towards prevention. Getting that definition of prevention is absolutely key. There are different mechanisms then of identifying that spend. The Scottish Government are currently looking at how you tag some spend as prevention—so, not necessarily creating a budget line but tagging it as 'preventative' and those definitions within preventative spend. We are exploring those options, with the key fundamental principle that transparency is key. Without us knowing what we're spending, how we're spending it, and, ultimately, what the outcomes of that spend are in terms of population health, it's not as impactful as it should be, and that's why I'm in this role. 

In terms of the weight loss medication, absolutely—it's creating that system of support around individuals for those lifestyle choices. They are right in some instances: preparing people for treatment in the NHS, for example, or certain body mass indexes. But making sure we've got that whole-system approach around the individual, to make sure there's a sustained improvement, is really important, and we're keeping that under review. Public Health Wales have been successful recently in co-ordinating a Wales-wide bid for funding through the obesity pathway innovation programme. That's £8 million of funding in order to look at these issues, to develop and test approaches that could form part of that delivery model going forward. We want to be looking at treating obesity as a chronic condition, and, obviously, the changes that would mean in terms of how the NHS would respond to that would be key. 

I've mentioned the food issue. On substance misuse, absolutely. I'm pleased to hear your approach in terms of the person-centred approach—not just dealing with the substance misuse issue, but, absolutely, mental health and making sure that all the services around that individual are there. Following on from the last Government's harm reduction method, we will absolutely be taking that forward and working closely with the Deputy Minister for mental health. If I've missed anything, as I know time is tight—[Interruption.] I'll come back to you on the COPD screening specifically. Thank you.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch am y cyfraniad ac am y croeso i'r rôl. O ran y trafodaethau dwyochrog a'r ddealltwriaeth a rennir gan y Llywodraeth, credaf mai dyma'r tro cyntaf i ni gael y drafodaeth hon ar draws lefel y Llywodraeth. Rwy'n credu bod llawer o enghreifftiau o arfer da wedi bod dros nifer o flynyddoedd, ond dim byd wedi'i ymgorffori, dim byd strategol, dim trafodaeth am effaith gwariant ar boblogaeth Cymru mewn meysydd portffolio eraill.

Felly, mae'r trafodaethau dwyochrog wedi bod yn dda iawn er mwyn cychwyn y broses honno o ran gweld lle gallwn weithio gyda'n gilydd. Er enghraifft, fe wnaethoch chi sôn am fwyd a thrafodaeth gyda'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros wydnwch gwledig. Nid trafodaeth ddwyochrog rhyngof fi a'r Gweinidog Cabinet hwnnw yw hynny'n unig; rydyn ni'n siarad am addysg, rydyn ni'n siarad am ein system gynllunio, rydyn ni'n siarad am yr economi a chefnogi ein busnesau bwyd. Felly, dyna beth mae'r dull hwn yn ymwneud ag ef yn llwyr, i wneud yn siŵr nad ydym yn colli'r cyfleoedd hynny. Ac os edrychwn ar y dull gweithredu o ran bwyd yn ystod y Llywodraeth ddiwethaf, roedd yn canolbwyntio'n eithaf cul, ac mae hyn yn adeiladu ar y gwaith y sonioch amdano gan eich cyd-Aelod blaenorol ar y Bil bwyd, i wneud yn siŵr ei fod yn ddull system gyfan.

Rwy'n cytuno'n llwyr â chi o ran ansawdd bwyd mewn ysgolion, ond hefyd addysgu ein pobl ifanc am sgiliau bwyd a gwneud yn siŵr ein bod yn deall o ble mae ein bwyd yn dod, cefnogi ein diwydiant amaethyddol gwych, ac edrych ar ein rheolau caffael. Felly, nid yw hyn yn rhywbeth ar gyfer bwyd yn unig; mae hyn yn ymwneud ag atal iechyd, gan edrych ar yr economi. Felly, mae'r trafodaethau dwyochrog hynny wedi cychwyn y drafodaeth honno wrth i ni weithio allan sut rydym yn gwneud yn siŵr bod y rhain yn cael trafodaethau wedi'u hymgorffori yn gynnar ym mhob datblygiad polisi—ein bod yn edrych ar atal o ran salwch a lleihau'r anghydraddoldeb iechyd sydd gennym a gwneud yn siŵr ei fod yn ddull traws-lywodraethol. A dyna fy rôl i—gwneud yn siŵr nad ydym yn colli'r cyfleoedd hynny wrth i ni weithio allan y fecaneg, a bod hynny'n cael ei ailadrodd ar lefel swyddogol hefyd. Nid yw'r sgyrsiau hyn, o bosibl, erioed wedi digwydd o'r blaen yn y meysydd polisi hyn, felly mae'n ymwneud â gwneud yn siŵr bod hynny'n cael ei ymgorffori fel ei bod yn systematig ac yn strategol ein bod yn edrych ar anghydraddoldeb iechyd ac yn edrych ar fesurau iechyd ataliol.

O ran y cyllidebau a'r costau, rydych chi'n codi rhai pwyntiau diddorol o ran sut y bydd hynny'n cael ei ddatblygu. Rydych chi'n gywir o ran llinell gyllideb newydd. Rwy'n credu mai'r cam cyntaf rydyn ni'n ymdrin ag ef nawr yw'r diffiniad o 'atal', yn enwedig os ydym wedi ymrwymo i fwy o wariant ar atal dros dymor y Senedd hon. Sut ydyn ni'n diffinio hynny yn wirioneddol bwysig—sut ydyn ni'n diffinio gweithgarwch cyfredol o fewn iechyd a gofal cymdeithasol, ond hefyd yn y meysydd portffolio eraill wrth i ni symud adnoddau tuag at atal. Mae cael y diffiniad hwnnw o atal yn hollol allweddol. Mae yna wahanol fecanweithiau wedyn ar gyfer nodi'r gwariant hwnnw. Mae Llywodraeth yr Alban ar hyn o bryd yn edrych i weld sut rydych chi'n labelu rhywfaint o wariant fel atal—felly, nid o reidrwydd yn creu llinell gyllideb ond ei labelu fel 'ataliol' a'r diffiniadau hynny o fewn gwariant ataliol. Rydym yn archwilio'r opsiynau hynny, gyda'r egwyddor sylfaenol allweddol bod tryloywder yn allweddol. Heb i ni wybod beth rydyn ni'n ei wario, sut rydyn ni'n ei wario, ac, yn y pen draw, beth yw canlyniadau'r gwariant hwnnw o ran iechyd y boblogaeth, nid yw mor effeithiol ag y dylai fod, a dyna pam rydw i yn y rôl hon.

O ran y feddyginiaeth colli pwysau, yn hollol—mae'n creu'r system honno o gefnogaeth o amgylch unigolion ar gyfer y dewisiadau ffordd o fyw hynny. Maen nhw'n iawn mewn rhai achosion: paratoi pobl ar gyfer triniaeth yn y GIG, er enghraifft, neu rai mynegeion màs y corff. Ond mae gwneud yn siŵr bod gennym y dull system gyfan hwnnw o amgylch yr unigolyn, i wneud yn siŵr bod gwelliant parhaus, yn bwysig iawn, ac rydym yn parhau i adolygu hynny. Mae Iechyd Cyhoeddus Cymru wedi bod yn llwyddiannus yn ddiweddar wrth gydlynu cais Cymru gyfan am gyllid drwy'r rhaglen arloesi llwybr gordewdra. Mae hynny'n £8 miliwn o gyllid er mwyn edrych ar y materion hyn, i ddatblygu a phrofi dulliau a allai fod yn rhan o'r model cyflawni hwnnw yn y dyfodol. Rydyn ni eisiau edrych ar drin gordewdra fel cyflwr cronig, ac, yn amlwg, byddai'r newidiadau yn sgil hynny o ran sut y byddai'r GIG yn ymateb i hynny yn allweddol.

Rwyf wedi sôn am y mater bwyd. O ran camddefnyddio sylweddau, yn hollol. Rwy'n falch o glywed am eich dull o ran y dull sy'n canolbwyntio ar y person—nid yn unig ymdrin â'r mater camddefnyddio sylweddau, ond, yn hollol, iechyd meddwl a gwneud yn siŵr bod yr holl wasanaethau o amgylch yr unigolyn hwnnw yno. Yn dilyn dull lleihau niwed y Llywodraeth ddiwethaf, byddwn yn bwrw ymlaen â hynny ac yn gweithio'n agos gyda'r Dirprwy Weinidog dros iechyd meddwl. Os ydw i wedi hepgor unrhyw beth, gan fy mod yn gwybod bod amser yn dynn— [Torri ar draws.] Byddaf yn dod yn ôl atoch chi ynghylch sgrinio COPD yn benodol. Diolch.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 6. Statement by the Deputy Minister for Public and Preventative Health: Priorities for Public and Preventative Health

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 6. Datganiad gan y Dirprwy Weinidog dros Iechyd Cyhoeddus ac Ataliol: Blaenoriaethau ar gyfer Iechyd Cyhoeddus ac Ataliol
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 6. Statement by the Deputy Minister for Public and Preventative Health: Priorities for Public and Preventative Health
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Thank you to the Deputy Minister for her statement today. As Welsh Labour's spokesperson, I welcome the cross-Government approach to preventative health, but I'm interested in what outcomes will be delivered for people across Wales. You've mentioned today the designated preventative departmental expenditure line within the Welsh budget for 2027-28, but I'm sure you'd agree, Minister, that it isn't just the creation of the budget line itself that we should be focused on, but rather how people's overall health and well-being will improve. I, like many others, challenge the Government to go beyond the process. We want to know what exactly will change and how success will be measured during this Senedd term.

I'm glad the Deputy Minister mentioned two very effective interventions: screening and vaccinations. It's good to hear the Deputy Minister supports the continuation of the national lung cancer screening programme, which was introduced by the Welsh Labour Government. I'm surprised there's no mention today of the HPV vaccine. Since it was introduced in 2008, the HPV vaccine has reduced cervical cancer rates by almost 90 per cent in women in their 20s, and that has saved hundreds of lives every year across the UK. So, I'd like to know how the Government will engage with schools across Wales to encourage participation in vaccination programmes like this.

Cervical screening also saves lives, and there's work to be done to make that more accessible. So, I'd like to see the Government learn from areas where there have been increases in screening uptake. You did give one example of screening uptake best practice, but I think there have been some other ones, particularly in London, where GPs have adapted to offer appointments for their clinics that fit in with people's work and family lives, such as on weekends and late evenings. So, I'd be interested to hear if you've been able to look into that.

Encouragement to help break down stigma is also key to increasing screening uptake. So, I'd like to know how Public Health Wales is focusing screening delivery that is tailored to local communities, for instance consistent breast screening opportunities in each geographical area throughout the year to support local health board demand. There's also work to be done engaging with businesses and organisations to support their workforce to attend all screening as a priority.

Targeted communications and education are important, breaking down stigma for everyone, but specifically for those attending their first screening appointment. We all know the way people access information is changing, and I'd like to know how national screening programmes are adapting to fit into those communication methods to reflect this.

Inclusion health is a globally recognised approach to address and prevent the health inequalities facing marginalised groups who struggle to access health services and experience far poorer health outcomes. We know that there's a huge human cost to these inequalities, as well as a cost to public services such as blue light services, A&E and emergency inpatient treatment. A stark example is people experiencing homelessness who experience acute physical and mental health problems and die 30 years younger than the general population.

There are some fantastic examples of inclusion health work led by Public Health Wales and services such as Cardiff and Vale inclusion service, and the partnership work between Ysbyty Gwynedd and Cyngor Sir Ynys Môn. However, this is often reliant on passionate individuals going above and beyond the remit of their roles, rather than inclusion health being prioritised, systematic and integrated with health services. Prioritising inclusion health is key to preventative health, as well as delivering significant savings to emergency health services. So, will you commit to making inclusion health one of your ministerial priorities, and consider developing an inclusion health strategy?

Finally, we know that sport helps to tackle obesity and to prevent physical and mental health conditions. Professional and grass-roots sport clubs play a leading role, and their impact is far-reaching. They are trusted places at the heart of our communities. I'd also recommend to you the Fit Fans programme, which works across our football league clubs. In Plaid Cymru's manifesto, you said you would invest in sports and physical activity as part of the preventative health agenda, and you've mentioned today your discussions with the Minister for culture and sport. However, any new work stream does need funding. The health minister couldn't give an answer when I previously asked how much that investment will be and where the money will come from. So, can you, Deputy Minister, today tell us that? Diolch.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch i'r Dirprwy Weinidog am ei datganiad heddiw. Fel llefarydd Llafur Cymru, rwy'n croesawu'r dull traws-lywodraethol o iechyd ataliol, ond mae gen i ddiddordeb ym mha ganlyniadau fydd yn cael eu cyflawni i bobl ledled Cymru. Rydych chi wedi sôn heddiw am y llinell gwariant adrannol ataliol dynodedig yng nghyllideb Cymru ar gyfer 2027-28, ond rwy'n siŵr y byddech chi'n cytuno, Weinidog, nad dim ond creu'r llinell gyllideb ei hun y dylem ganolbwyntio arno, ond yn hytrach sut y bydd iechyd a llesiant cyffredinol pobl yn gwella. Rwyf i, fel llawer o rai eraill, yn herio'r Llywodraeth i fynd y tu hwnt i'r broses. Rydym eisiau gwybod beth yn union fydd yn newid a sut y bydd llwyddiant yn cael ei fesur yn ystod tymor y Senedd hon.

Rwy'n falch bod y Dirprwy Weinidog wedi sôn am ddwy ymyrraeth effeithiol iawn: sgrinio a brechiadau. Mae'n dda clywed bod y Dirprwy Weinidog yn cefnogi parhad y rhaglen sgrinio canser yr ysgyfaint genedlaethol, a gyflwynwyd gan Lywodraeth Lafur Cymru. Rwy'n synnu nad oes sôn heddiw am y brechlyn HPV. Ers iddo gael ei gyflwyno yn 2008, mae'r brechlyn HPV wedi lleihau cyfraddau canser ceg y groth bron i 90 y cant mewn menywod yn eu 20au, ac mae hynny wedi achub cannoedd o fywydau bob blwyddyn ledled y DU. Felly, hoffwn wybod sut y bydd y Llywodraeth yn ymgysylltu ag ysgolion ledled Cymru i annog cyfranogiad mewn rhaglenni brechu fel hon.

Mae sgrinio ceg y groth hefyd yn achub bywydau, ac mae gwaith i'w wneud i wneud hynny'n fwy hygyrch. Felly, hoffwn weld y Llywodraeth yn dysgu o feysydd lle bu cynnydd yn y defnydd o sgrinio. Fe wnaethoch chi roi un enghraifft o arfer gorau sgrinio, ond rwy'n credu bod rhai eraill, yn enwedig yn Llundain, lle mae meddygon teulu wedi addasu i gynnig apwyntiadau ar gyfer eu clinigau sy'n cyd-fynd â bywydau gwaith a theuluol pobl, megis ar benwythnosau a hwyr gyda'r nos. Felly, byddai gen i ddiddordeb clywed os ydych chi wedi gallu edrych i mewn i hynny.

Mae anogaeth i helpu i chwalu stigma hefyd yn allweddol i gynyddu'r nifer sy'n manteisio ar sgrinio. Felly, hoffwn wybod sut mae Iechyd Cyhoeddus Cymru yn canolbwyntio ar ddarparu sgrinio sydd wedi'i deilwra i gymunedau lleol, er enghraifft cyfleoedd sgrinio'r fron cyson ym mhob ardal ddaearyddol drwy gydol y flwyddyn i gefnogi'r galw ar fyrddau iechyd lleol. Mae yna waith i'w wneud hefyd wrth ymgysylltu â busnesau a sefydliadau i gefnogi eu gweithlu i fynychu pob sgrinio fel blaenoriaeth.

Mae cyfathrebu ac addysg wedi'i dargedu yn bwysig, gan chwalu stigma i bawb, ond yn benodol i'r rhai sy'n mynychu eu hapwyntiad sgrinio cyntaf. Rydyn ni i gyd yn gwybod bod y ffordd y mae pobl yn cael mynediad at wybodaeth yn newid, a hoffwn wybod sut mae rhaglenni sgrinio cenedlaethol yn addasu er mwyn bod yn addas ar gyfer y dulliau cyfathrebu hynny i adlewyrchu hyn.

Mae iechyd cynhwysiant yn ddull a gydnabyddir yn fyd-eang o fynd i'r afael â'r anghydraddoldebau iechyd sy'n wynebu grwpiau ymylol sy'n cael trafferth cael mynediad at wasanaethau iechyd ac sy'n profi canlyniadau iechyd llawer gwaeth. Rydym yn gwybod bod cost ddynol enfawr i'r anghydraddoldebau hyn, yn ogystal â chost i wasanaethau cyhoeddus fel gwasanaethau golau glas, damweiniau ac achosion brys a thriniaeth cleifion mewnol brys. Enghraifft amlwg yw pobl sy'n profi digartrefedd sy'n profi problemau iechyd corfforol a meddyliol acíwt ac sy'n marw 30 mlynedd yn iau na'r boblogaeth gyffredinol.

Mae yna enghreifftiau gwych o waith iechyd cynhwysiant dan arweiniad Iechyd Cyhoeddus Cymru a gwasanaethau fel gwasanaeth cynhwysiant Caerdydd a'r Fro, a'r gwaith partneriaeth rhwng Ysbyty Gwynedd a Chyngor Sir Ynys Môn. Fodd bynnag, mae hyn yn aml yn dibynnu ar unigolion angerddol sy'n mynd y tu hwnt i gylch gwaith eu rolau, yn hytrach na chynhwysiant iechyd yn cael ei flaenoriaethu, yn systematig ac yn cael ei integreiddio â gwasanaethau iechyd. Mae blaenoriaethu iechyd cynhwysiant yn allweddol i iechyd ataliol, yn ogystal â darparu arbedion sylweddol i wasanaethau iechyd brys. Felly, a fyddwch chi'n ymrwymo i wneud iechyd cynhwysiant yn un o'ch blaenoriaethau gweinidogol, ac ystyried datblygu strategaeth iechyd cynhwysiant?

Yn olaf, gwyddom fod chwaraeon yn helpu i fynd i'r afael â gordewdra ac i atal cyflyrau iechyd corfforol a meddyliol. Mae clybiau chwaraeon proffesiynol a llawr gwlad yn chwarae rôl flaenllaw, ac mae eu heffaith yn bellgyrhaeddol. Maen nhw'n lleoedd dibynadwy yng nghanol ein cymunedau. Byddwn hefyd yn argymell i chi y rhaglen Fit Fans, sy'n gweithio ar draws ein clybiau cynghrair pêl-droed. Ym maniffesto Plaid Cymru, dywedoch y byddech yn buddsoddi mewn chwaraeon a gweithgarwch corfforol fel rhan o'r agenda iechyd ataliol, ac rydych wedi sôn heddiw am eich trafodaethau gyda'r Gweinidog dros ddiwylliant a chwaraeon. Fodd bynnag, mae angen cyllid ar unrhyw ffrwd waith newydd. Ni allai'r Gweinidog dros iechyd roi ateb pan ofynnais i o'r blaen faint fydd y buddsoddiad hwnnw ac o ble y bydd yr arian yn dod. Felly, a allwch chi, Ddirprwy Weinidog, ddweud hynny wrthym heddiw? Diolch.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 6. Datganiad gan y Dirprwy Weinidog dros Iechyd Cyhoeddus ac Ataliol: Blaenoriaethau ar gyfer Iechyd Cyhoeddus ac Ataliol
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 6. Statement by the Deputy Minister for Public and Preventative Health: Priorities for Public and Preventative Health
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Diolch. Thanks for those questions. In terms of the outcomes, we're going to be working on a public health strategy that brings all of this together in terms of what we're trying to achieve across portfolios, and looking at those objectives and those outcomes in the short, medium and longer term. As you mentioned, in terms of the budget, the budget increases transparency on what's actually happening. We don't have that now. Over the last 27 years, we don't know what's been spent on prevention. We don't know the impact. It has not been embedded. So, ensuring that we have transparency in terms of what we're spending does drive activity in terms of being transparent and putting those outcome measures in place to make sure that we are really clear what the expectation is in terms of public and preventative health.

In terms of the HPV vaccine, absolutely, and there will be a statement by the Cabinet Minister on the cancer strategy this week, which will include details on that.

You're right in terms of working with education, and we've been discussing with the Cabinet Minister for education how we can improve those messages to schools. Schools are under pressure with lots of demands on their time, but making sure that they understand their role in promoting vaccine uptake in schools is really important, and something that we are working on.

One of the things that worries me is the differences within our deprived communities in terms of screening and vaccine uptake. The work you mentioned there on inclusion health is really important. There hasn't been a systematic look at this up until now. So, we really need to be making sure that the work that Public Health Wales are doing on screening and vaccinations really understands at that community level what the barriers are for uptake in terms of screening and vaccination. Because we know the benefits of making sure that people undertake screening and vaccination when they're meant to be part of that. 

So, there is definitely good work happening, especially on the stigma side as well, but we do need to do more. We do need to better understand it, and we do need to better make sure that the good work that's happening now is better understood across the health service as well.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch am y cwestiynau yna. O ran y canlyniadau, rydyn ni'n mynd i weithio ar strategaeth iechyd cyhoeddus sy'n dod â hyn i gyd at ei gilydd o ran yr hyn rydyn ni'n ceisio ei gyflawni ar draws portffolios, ac edrych ar yr amcanion hynny a'r canlyniadau hynny yn y tymor byr, canolig a hirach. Fel y soniwyd gennych, o ran y gyllideb, mae'r gyllideb yn cynyddu tryloywder o ran yr hyn sy'n digwydd mewn gwirionedd. Nid yw hynny gennym ni nawr. Dros y 27 mlynedd diwethaf, nid ydym yn gwybod beth sydd wedi'i wario ar atal. Nid ydym yn gwybod beth yw'r effaith. Nid yw wedi cael ei ymgorffori. Felly, mae sicrhau bod gennym dryloywder o ran yr hyn rydyn ni'n ei wario yn ysgogi gweithgarwch o ran bod yn dryloyw a rhoi'r mesurau canlyniadau hynny ar waith i wneud yn siŵr ein bod yn glir iawn beth yw'r disgwyliad o ran iechyd y cyhoedd ac ataliol.

O ran y brechlyn HPV, yn sicr, a bydd datganiad gan y Gweinidog Cabinet ar y strategaeth ganser yr wythnos hon, a fydd yn cynnwys manylion am hynny.

Rydych chi'n iawn o ran gweithio gydag addysg, ac rydym wedi bod yn trafod gyda'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros addysg sut y gallwn wella'r negeseuon hynny i ysgolion. Mae ysgolion dan bwysau gyda llawer o ofynion ar eu hamser, ond mae gwneud yn siŵr eu bod yn deall eu rôl wrth hyrwyddo defnydd o frechlynnau mewn ysgolion yn bwysig iawn, ac yn rhywbeth rydyn ni'n gweithio arno.

Un o'r pethau sy'n fy mhoeni yw'r gwahaniaethau o fewn ein cymunedau difreintiedig o ran sgrinio a chymryd brechlynnau. Mae'r gwaith y sonioch amdano ar iechyd cynhwysiant yn bwysig iawn. Nid oes golwg systematig ar hyn hyd yn hyn. Felly, mae angen i ni fod yn siŵr bod y gwaith y mae Iechyd Cyhoeddus Cymru yn ei wneud ar sgrinio a brechiadau yn deall ar y lefel gymunedol honno beth yw'r rhwystrau ar gyfer eu defnyddio o ran sgrinio a brechu. Oherwydd rydyn ni'n gwybod beth yw'r manteision o wneud yn siŵr bod pobl yn ymgymryd â sgrinio a brechu pan fyddant i fod yn rhan o hynny. 

Felly, mae yna waith da yn digwydd, yn enwedig ar yr ochr stigma hefyd, ond mae angen i ni wneud mwy. Mae angen i ni ei ddeall yn well, ac mae angen i ni wneud yn siŵr bod y gwaith da sy'n digwydd nawr yn cael ei ddeall yn well ar draws y gwasanaeth iechyd hefyd.
